title.zh: 卷九十一 列傳第四十一: 桓彥範 敬暉 崔玄暐 張柬之 袁恕己
title.en: Volume 91 Biographies 41: Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, Cui Xuanwei, Zhang Jianzhi, Yuan Shuji
title.raw: 卷九十一 列傳第四十一: 桓彥範 敬暉 崔玄暐 張柬之 袁恕己 Volume 91 Biographies 41: Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, Cui Xuanwei, Zhang Jianzhi, Yuan Shuji

sentences.zh: 桓彥範敬暉崔玄暐張柬之袁恕己

translations.literal: Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, Cui Xuanwei, Zhang Jianzhi, Yuan Shuji
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, Cui Xuanwei, Zhang Jianzhi, and Yuan Shuji

sentences.zh: 桓彥範，潤州曲阿人也。

translations.literal: Huan Yanfan was a native of Qu'e in Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yanfan came from Qu'e in Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖法嗣，雍王府諮議參軍、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fasi was advisory staff officer of the Prince of Yong's household and a scholar of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fasi had served as advisory staff officer to the Prince of Yong and as a scholar of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 彥範慷慨俊爽，少以門蔭調補右翊衛。

translations.literal: Yanfan was magnanimous, handsome, and spirited; in youth he was appointed to the Right Yiwu Guard through hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan was openhanded, handsome, and quick of spirit; in his youth he entered service in the Right Yiwu Guard by hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 聖曆初，累除司衛寺主簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shengli era he was repeatedly promoted to chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shengli era he rose through successive appointments to chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 納言狄仁傑特相禮異，嚐謂曰：“足下才識如是，必能自致遠大。

translations.literal: The Counselor Di Renjie treated him with special courtesy and once said to him, "Your talent and insight are such that you will surely attain great eminence on your own."
translations.idiomatic: Counselor Di Renjie singled him out for unusual respect and once told him, "With talent and insight like yours, you are bound to rise far on your own merit."

sentences.zh: ”尋擢授監察御史。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward he was promoted and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he was elevated to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 長安三年，曆遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chang'an he was promoted in succession to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chang'an he advanced step by step to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 四年，轉司刑少卿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 時司仆卿張昌宗坐遣術人李弘泰占己有天分，御史中丞宋璟請收付製獄，窮理其罪，則天不許。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud Zhang Changzong was implicated for sending the technician Li Hongtai to divine that he possessed the Mandate of Heaven; the vice censor-in-chief Song Jing requested that he be taken into the imperial prison and his crime thoroughly investigated, but Empress Wu did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Vice Minister Zhang Changzong stood accused of sending the occultist Li Hongtai to divine that he was destined for the throne; Vice Censor-in-Chief Song Jing asked that he be placed in the imperial prison and his crime fully prosecuted, but the Empress Dowager refused.

sentences.zh: 彥範上疏曰：

translations.literal: Yanfan submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan memorialized the throne as follows:

sentences.zh: 昌宗無德無才，謬承恩寵，自宜粉骨碎肌，以答殊造，豈得苞藏禍心，有此占相？

translations.literal: Changzong is without virtue or talent yet has wrongly received your favor; he ought to grind his bones to powder to repay your extraordinary grace—how can he harbor a treacherous heart and undertake such divination of his fate?
translations.idiomatic: Changzong lacks both virtue and ability, yet he has been showered with favor; he ought to offer his body to the ground to repay your extraordinary grace. How can he conceal treason in his heart and seek such a reading of his destiny?

sentences.zh: 陛下以簪履恩久，不忍加刑；

translations.literal: Your Majesty, because of long-standing favor as close attendant, is unwilling to impose punishment;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, out of long affection for a close attendant, is unwilling to punish him;

sentences.zh: 昌宗以逆亂罪多，自招其咎。

translations.literal: Changzong, through his many crimes of rebellion, has brought calamity upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: Changzong, by his many acts of treason, has brought judgment upon himself.

sentences.zh: 此是皇天降怒，非唯陛下故誅。

translations.literal: This is Heaven above sending down wrath; it is not merely Your Majesty deliberately executing him.
translations.idiomatic: This is Heaven itself showing anger—it is not simply Your Majesty choosing to execute him.

sentences.zh: 違天不祥，乞陛下裁擇。

translations.literal: To defy Heaven is inauspicious; I beg Your Majesty to decide.
translations.idiomatic: To go against Heaven is ill-omened; I beg Your Majesty to judge accordingly.

sentences.zh: 原其本奏，以防事敗。

translations.literal: Examining his original memorial, it was to guard against failure of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: If one traces his original report, it was written to guard against the plot's failure.

sentences.zh: 事敗即言奏訖，不敗則候時為逆。

translations.literal: If the affair failed he would say the memorial had been submitted and finished; if it did not fail he would wait for the right moment to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: If the plot failed, he would claim the memorial had already been filed and closed; if it did not fail, he would bide his time to rebel.

sentences.zh: 此乃奸臣詭計，疑惑聖心，今果遂其所謀，陛下何忍不察？

translations.literal: This is the treacherous minister's deceitful scheme to confuse the sage heart; now he has indeed accomplished what he plotted—how can Your Majesty bear not to investigate?
translations.idiomatic: This was the traitor's ruse to cloud Your Majesty's judgment; he has now carried out exactly what he planned—how can Your Majesty still refuse to see it?

sentences.zh: 若昌宗無此占相，奏後不合更與弘泰往還，尚令修福，復擬禳厄，此則期於必遂，元無悔心。

translations.literal: If Changzong had not undertaken this divination, after the memorial it would not have been fitting for him again to associate with Hongtai, still to have blessings performed, and again to plan averting calamity—this shows he expected certain success and originally had no heart of repentance.
translations.idiomatic: If Changzong had not sought this divination, after submitting his report he ought not to have resumed dealings with Hongtai, commissioned merit rituals, and planned further rites to avert disaster—this shows he meant to succeed at all costs and never intended to repent.

sentences.zh: 縱雖奏聞，情實難恕，此而可舍，誰其可刑？

translations.literal: Even if he reported it, the facts are hard to forgive; if this may be spared, who may be punished?
translations.idiomatic: Even if he did report it, the facts are unpardonable; if this man may be spared, who deserves execution?

sentences.zh: 況經兩度事彰，天恩並垂舍宥，昌宗自為得計，人亦以為應運，即不勞兵甲，天下皆從，萬方譏之，以為陛下縱成其亂也。

translations.literal: Moreover, after two occasions when the matter was exposed, Heaven's grace both times extended pardon; Changzong himself thought he had succeeded in his plan, and people also thought he answered to destiny—then without troubling arms, all under Heaven would follow, and the myriad regions would mock, thinking Your Majesty was allowing his rebellion to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, after the affair had been exposed twice and imperial mercy spared him both times, Changzong believed his scheme was working and the people took it as Heaven's will—then without raising an army, the realm would follow him, and all the world would say Your Majesty was letting his rebellion succeed.

sentences.zh: 君在，臣圖天分，是為逆臣，不誅，社稷亡矣。

translations.literal: While the ruler lives, a subject plots for Heaven's portion—this is a rebellious minister; if he is not executed, the altars of state will perish.
translations.idiomatic: While the sovereign still reigns, a subject plots to seize the Mandate—such a man is a traitor; if he is not put to death, the dynasty will fall.

sentences.zh: 伏請付鸞台鳳閣三司考竟其罪。

translations.literal: I humbly request that he be handed over to the three offices of the Luan Terrace and Phoenix Pavilion to investigate his crime to the end.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that he be referred to the tripartite offices of the Luan Terrace and Phoenix Pavilion for a full investigation of his crime.

sentences.zh: 疏奏不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 時又內史李嶠等奏稱：“往屬革命之時，人多逆節，鞫訊決斷，刑獄至嚴，刻薄之吏，恣行酷法。

translations.literal: At that time the Palace Secretary Li Qiao and others also memorialized, saying, "In former times, during the dynastic change, many people showed rebellious conduct; interrogation and judgment were extremely severe, and harsh officials wantonly applied cruel laws."
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Palace Secretary Li Qiao and others memorialized, saying, "During the recent change of dynasty many people were charged with disloyalty; trials were harsh and unforgiving, and cruel officials applied the law as they pleased."

sentences.zh: 其周興、丘勣、來俊臣所劾破家者，並請雪免。

translations.literal: Those whose families were ruined through impeachment by Zhou Xing, Qiu Ji, and Lai Junchen—I request that all be cleared and pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: All those whose families were destroyed through prosecutions by Zhou Xing, Qiu Ji, and Lai Junchen should be cleared and restored."

sentences.zh: ”彥範又奏請自文明元年以後得罪人，除揚、豫、博三州及諸謀逆魁首，一切赦之。

translations.literal: " Yanfan again memorialized requesting that from the first year of Wenming onward all who had been punished, except those in Yang, Yu, and Bo prefectures and the ringleaders of various treason plots, be entirely amnestied.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanfan also asked that everyone punished since the first year of Wenming be pardoned, except persons in Yang, Yu, and Bo prefectures and the chief conspirators in treason cases.

sentences.zh: 表疏前後十奏，辭旨激切，至是方見允納。

translations.literal: His memorials were submitted ten times in all, their wording fierce and urgent; only then was approval granted.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorial after memorial—ten in all—with language sharp and urgent; only then was his request accepted.

sentences.zh: 彥範凡所奏議，若逢人主詰責，則辭色無懼，爭之愈厲。

translations.literal: In all memorial proposals Yanfan made, if the ruler rebuked him he showed no fear in expression and argued all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yanfan memorialized on policy and the ruler rebuked him, he showed no fear in word or face and pressed his argument all the harder.

sentences.zh: 又嚐謂所親曰：“今既躬為大理，人命所懸，必不能順旨詭辭，以求苟免。

translations.literal: He also once said to those close to him, "Now that I personally hold the office of chief justice, upon which human lives hang, I surely cannot follow the ruler's intent with deceitful words to seek a careless escape."
translations.idiomatic: He also once told his intimates, "Now that I hold the chief justiceship, with men's lives in the balance, I cannot twist my words to the ruler's liking merely to save myself."

sentences.zh: 是歲冬，則天不豫。

translations.literal: That winter the Empress Dowager fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Empress Wu fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 張易之與弟昌宗入閣侍疾，潛圖逆亂。

translations.literal: Zhang Yizhi and his younger brother Changzong entered the inner apartments to attend her illness and secretly plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yizhi and his brother Changzong entered the inner palace to nurse her and secretly plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣侍郎張柬之與桓彥範及中台右丞敬暉等建策將誅之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion Zhang Jianzhi, together with Huan Yanfan and the Right Vice Director of the Central Secretariat Jing Hui and others, devised a plan to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zhang Jianzhi, Huan Yanfan, Right Vice Director Jing Hui, and others formed a plan to put them to death.

sentences.zh: 柬之遽引彥範及暉並為左右羽林將軍，委以禁兵，共圖其事。

translations.literal: Jianzhi promptly had Yanfan and Hui both appointed generals of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Armies, entrusted them with the forbidden troops, and together plotted the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi quickly had Yanfan and Hui appointed generals of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Armies, placed the palace guard under their command, and joined them in plotting the coup.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子每於北門起居，彥範與暉因得謁見，密陳其計，太子從之。

translations.literal: At that time the Crown Prince daily attended court at the north gate; Yanfan and Hui thus obtained audience, secretly laid out their plan, and the Crown Prince assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince was then attending court daily at the north gate; Yanfan and Hui seized the chance to see him, laid out their plan in secret, and won his consent.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年正月，彥範與敬暉及左羽林將軍李湛、李多祚、右羽林將軍楊元琰、左威衛將軍薛思行等，率左右羽林兵及千騎五百餘人討易之、昌宗於宮中，令李湛、李多祚就東宮迎皇太子。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Shenlong, Yanfan and Jing Hui, together with the Left Forest of Feathers generals Li Zhan and Li Duozuo, the Right Forest of Feathers general Yang Yuanyan, the Left Weiwu Guard general Xue Sixing, and others, led more than five hundred troops of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Armies and the Thousand Riders to attack Yizhi and Changzong in the palace, and ordered Li Zhan and Li Duozuo to go to the Eastern Palace to welcome the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Shenlong, Yanfan and Jing Hui, with Left Forest generals Li Zhan and Li Duozuo, Right Forest general Yang Yuanyan, Left Weiwu general Xue Sixing, and others, led more than five hundred men of the palace guards and the Thousand Riders to strike down Yizhi and Changzong inside the palace, while Li Zhan and Li Duozuo were sent to the Eastern Palace to bring out the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 兵至玄武門，彥範等奉太子斬關而入，兵士大噪。

translations.literal: When the troops reached the Xuanwu Gate, Yanfan and the others, escorting the Crown Prince, cut through the gate and entered; the soldiers raised a great clamor.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xuanwu Gate Yanfan and his party, escorting the Crown Prince, forced the gate and entered amid a great uproar from the troops.

sentences.zh: 時則天在迎仙宮之集仙殿。

translations.literal: At that time the Empress Dowager was in the Hall of Assembled Immortals of the Palace of Welcoming Immortals.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was then in the Hall of Assembled Immortals in the Palace of Welcoming Immortals.

sentences.zh: 斬易之、昌宗於廓下，並就第斬其兄汴州刺史昌期、司禮少卿同休，並梟首於天津橋南。

translations.literal: Yizhi and Changzong were beheaded beneath the corridor; at their residences their elder brother, Bian Prefecture prefect Changqi, and the Vice Minister of Rites Tongxiu were also beheaded, and all their heads were displayed south of the Tianjin Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi and Changzong were beheaded under the eaves; at their homes their elder brother Changqi, prefect of Bian, and Tongxiu, vice minister of rites, were also killed, and all their heads were exposed south of the Tianjin Bridge.

sentences.zh: 士庶見者，莫不歡叫相賀，或臠割其肉，一夕都盡。

translations.literal: Commoners and officials who saw it none failed to shout in joy and congratulate one another; some cut their flesh in pieces, and in one night it was all gone.
translations.idiomatic: Every commoner and official who saw it shouted for joy; some hacked their flesh to pieces, and within a single night nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 明日，太子即位，彥範以功加銀青光祿大夫，拜納言，賜勳上柱國，封譙郡公，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: The next day the Crown Prince took the throne; for his merit Yanfan was given the additional title Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, appointed Counselor, granted the merit rank Pillar of the State Upper First Class, enfeoffed as Duke of Qiao commandery, and granted five hundred households of actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Crown Prince ascended the throne; for his service Yanfan was promoted to Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, made Counselor, granted the merit rank Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as Duke of Qiao, and given a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又改為侍中，從新令也。

translations.literal: He was again changed to Attendant-in-Chief, following the new statutes.
translations.idiomatic: His title was then changed to Attendant-in-Chief, in accordance with the new regulations.

sentences.zh: 彥範嚐表論時政數條，其大略曰：“昔孔子論《詩》以《關雎》為始，言后妃者人倫之本，理亂之端也。

translations.literal: Yanfan once submitted a memorial discussing several points of current policy; its general purport said, "Formerly Confucius discussed the Odes and took Guan Ju as the beginning, saying that the empress and consorts are the root of human relations and the starting point of order and disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan once memorialized on several points of current policy, writing in substance, "Confucius taught that the Odes begin with Guan Ju because the empress and consorts are the foundation of human relations and the source of order or chaos."

sentences.zh: 故皇、英降而虞道興，任、姒歸而姬宗盛。

translations.literal: Therefore when Huang and Ying descended, the way of Yu flourished; when Ren and Si returned, the house of Ji prospered.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang and Ying came down, the way of Yu rose; when Ren and Si were wed, the house of Zhou flourished.

sentences.zh: 桀奔南巢，禍階妹喜，魯桓滅國，惑以齊媛。

translations.literal: Jie fled to Southern Nest—the calamity began with Mo Xi; Duke Huan of Lu lost his state—he was deluded by the lady of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Jie fled to Southern Nest because disaster began with Mo Xi; Duke Huan of Lu lost his state because he was bewitched by a woman of Qi.

sentences.zh: 伏見陛下每臨朝聽政，皇后必施帷幔坐於殿上，預聞政事。

translations.literal: I observe that whenever Your Majesty attends court to hear government, the empress invariably hangs a curtain and sits upon the hall, taking part in advance in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that whenever Your Majesty holds court, the empress always sits behind a curtain on the dais and takes part in government beforehand.

sentences.zh: 臣愚曆選列辟，詳求往代，帝王有與婦人謀及政者，莫不破國亡身，傾輈繼路。

translations.literal: This foolish subject has repeatedly examined the ranks of rulers and closely sought out past ages: whenever emperors deliberated on government with women, none failed to lose state and body, with ruin following ruin in succession.
translations.idiomatic: I have surveyed ruler after ruler and searched the past in detail: whenever an emperor took counsel on government from a woman, state and life were lost, and ruin followed ruin without end.

sentences.zh: 且以陰乘陽，違天也，以婦淩夫，違人也。

translations.literal: Moreover, for yin to ride upon yang is to defy Heaven; for a wife to tower over her husband is to defy humanity.
translations.idiomatic: For yin to dominate yang is to defy Heaven; for a wife to rule over her husband is to defy human order.

sentences.zh: 違天不祥，違人不義。

translations.literal: To defy Heaven is inauspicious; to defy humanity is unrighteous.
translations.idiomatic: To defy Heaven brings ill fortune; to defy human order is unjust.

sentences.zh: 由是古人譬以‘牝雞之晨，惟家之索。

translations.literal: Hence the ancients likened it to 'when the hen crows at dawn, the household is undone.'
translations.idiomatic: That is why the ancients said, 'When the hen crows at dawn, the household is ruined.'

sentences.zh: ’《易》曰‘無攸遂，在中饋’，言婦人不得預於國政也。

translations.literal: ' The Changes says, 'Nothing is to be furthered; attend to provisions within,' meaning that women must not take part in national government.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Book of Changes says, 'Nothing is to be furthered; keep to the inner household,' meaning that women must not intervene in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下覽古人之言，察古人之意，上以社稷為重，下以蒼生在念。

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty to review the words of the ancients and discern their intent, taking the altars of state as paramount above and keeping the common people in mind below.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to read the words of the ancients and grasp their meaning, putting the altars of state first and the welfare of the people foremost.

sentences.zh: 宜令皇后無往正殿干預外朝，專在中宮，聿修陰教，則坤儀式固，鼎命惟永。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should order the empress not to go to the main hall to interfere in the outer court, but to remain solely in the inner palace and diligently cultivate feminine instruction—then the queenly rites will be secure and the tripod mandate ever enduring.
translations.idiomatic: The empress should be kept from the main hall and from meddling in outer-court affairs; let her remain in the inner palace and devote herself to women's instruction—then the queenly order will stand firm and the dynasty endure.

sentences.zh: 又曰：“臣聞京師喧喧，道路籍籍，皆云胡僧慧範矯托佛教，詭惑后妃，故得出入禁闈，撓亂時政。

translations.literal: He also said, "I hear the capital clamorous and the roads abuzz, all saying that the foreign monk Huifan falsely relied on Buddhism to deceive and bewitch the empress and consorts, and thus gained entry to the forbidden inner quarters and disturbed current government."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "I hear the capital in an uproar and the streets full of talk, all saying that the foreign monk Huifan uses Buddhism as a pretense to delude the empress and consorts, and so comes and goes within the forbidden quarters and meddles in government."

sentences.zh: 陛下又輕騎微行，數幸其室，上下媟黷，有虧尊嚴。

translations.literal: Your Majesty again goes lightly mounted in plain dress and frequently visits his dwelling; superior and inferior are licentious and irreverent, to the detriment of dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty also rides out lightly disguised and visits his house again and again; such familiarity between sovereign and subject diminishes imperial dignity.

sentences.zh: 臣抑嚐聞興化致理，必由進善；

translations.literal: This subject has also heard that to raise transformation and attain good government must proceed through advancing the good;
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that to bring about good order one must advance the worthy;

sentences.zh: 康國寧人，莫大棄惡。

translations.literal: to secure the state and pacify the people, nothing is greater than casting off evil.
translations.idiomatic: and to secure the realm and settle the people, nothing matters more than casting out evil.

sentences.zh: 故孔子曰：‘執左道以亂政者殺，假鬼神以危人者殺。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius said, 'Those who hold heterodox ways to disturb government are to be killed; those who borrow ghosts and spirits to endanger people are to be killed.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'Those who use heterodox ways to disturb government shall be put to death; those who invoke spirits to harm others shall be put to death.'

sentences.zh: ’今慧範之罪，不殊於此也。

translations.literal: ' Huifan's crime today is no different from this.
translations.idiomatic: ' Huifan's crimes are no different.

sentences.zh: 若不急誅，必生變亂。

translations.literal: If he is not urgently executed, rebellion will surely arise.
translations.idiomatic: If he is not executed at once, turmoil will surely follow.

sentences.zh: 除惡務本，去邪勿疑，實願天聰，早加裁貶。

translations.literal: In removing evil one must strike at the root; in casting out wickedness one must not hesitate—I truly wish Heaven's discernment would soon impose judgment and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: When rooting out evil one must strike at the source; when removing wickedness one must not hesitate. I earnestly beg Your Majesty's wise judgment to punish him without delay.

sentences.zh: ”疏奏不納。

translations.literal: " The memorial was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was rejected.

sentences.zh: 時有墨敕授方術人鄭普思秘書監，葉淨能國子祭酒，彥範苦言其不可。

translations.literal: At that time an ink edict appointed the technician Zheng Pusi Director of the Secretariat and Ye Jingneng Libationer of the Directorate of Education; Yanfan bitterly argued that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: An informal edict then appointed the occultist Zheng Pusi Director of the Secretariat and Ye Jingneng Libationer of the Directorate of Education; Yanfan protested strenuously that this must not stand.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“既要用之，無容便止。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Since I am already going to employ them, there is no room to stop at once."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Since I mean to use them, there is no question of stopping now."

sentences.zh: ”彥範又對曰：“陛下自龍飛寶位，遽下製云：‘軍國政化，皆依貞觀故事。

translations.literal: " Yanfan replied again, "Since Your Majesty ascended the precious throne, you promptly issued a regulation saying, 'Military and civil government and transformation shall all follow the precedents of the Zhenguan era.'"
translations.idiomatic: " Yanfan replied, "When Your Majesty first took the throne, you issued a decree that military and civil administration should follow the precedents of the Zhenguan reign."

sentences.zh: ’昔貞觀中嚐以魏徵、虞世南、顏師古為秘書監，孔穎達為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: ' In Zhenguan Wei Zheng, Yu Shinan, and Yan Shigu were once made Directors of the Secretariat, and Kong Yingda was made Libationer of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: ' In Zhenguan Wei Zheng, Yu Shinan, and Yan Shigu served as Directors of the Secretariat, and Kong Yingda as Libationer of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 至如普思等是方伎庸流，豈足以比蹤前烈？

translations.literal: As for Pusi and the like, they are vulgar practitioners of occult arts—how can they be compared with those former worthies?
translations.idiomatic: Men like Pusi are mere street occultists—how can they be compared with those great predecessors?

sentences.zh: 臣恐物議謂陛下官不擇才，濫以天秩加於私愛。

translations.literal: I fear public discussion will say Your Majesty does not choose talent for office but recklessly bestows Heaven's ranks upon private favorites.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the world will say Your Majesty appoints office without regard to talent and lavishes imperial rank on personal favorites.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下少加慎擇。

translations.literal: I only wish Your Majesty to be somewhat more careful in selection.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to choose your appointees with greater care.

sentences.zh: ”帝竟不納。

translations.literal: " The Emperor in the end did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 時韋皇后既幹朝政，德靜郡王武三思又居中用事，以則天為彥範等所廢，常深憤怨，又慮彥範等漸除武氏，乃先事圖之。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Wei already interfered in court government, and Prince Dejing Wu Sansi again held power at the center; because Empress Wu had been deposed by Yanfan and the others, he constantly harbored deep resentment and also feared that Yanfan and the others would gradually eliminate the Wu clan—therefore he plotted against them first.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei was already meddling in government, and Prince Dejing Wu Sansi again held sway at court; because Empress Wu had been overthrown by Yanfan and his allies, he nursed a deep grudge and feared they would gradually destroy the Wu clan—so he moved against them first.

sentences.zh: 皇后韋氏既雅為帝所信寵，言無不從，三思又私通於韋氏，乃日夕讒毀彥範等。

translations.literal: Empress Wei had long been trusted and favored by the Emperor, and he never failed to follow her words; Sansi also had secret relations with the Wei clan, and day and night slandered Yanfan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei had long enjoyed the emperor's trust, and he never refused her counsel; Sansi was also carrying on a secret affair with her, and day and night he slandered Yanfan and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 帝竟用三思計，進封彥範為扶陽郡王、敬暉為平陽郡五、張柬之為漢陽郡五、崔玄暐為博陵郡王、袁恕己為南陽郡王，並加特進，令罷知政事。

translations.literal: The Emperor finally adopted Sansi's plan, promoting Yanfan to Prince of Fuyang commandery, Jing Hui to Prince of Pingyang commandery, Zhang Jianzhi to Prince of Hanyang commandery, Cui Xuanwei to Prince of Boling commandery, and Yuan Shuji to Prince of Nanyang commandery, all with the additional title of Special Advancement, and ordering them to cease participation in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at last took Sansi's advice, ennobling Yanfan as Prince of Fuyang, Jing Hui as Prince of Pingyang, Zhang Jianzhi as Prince of Hanyang, Cui Xuanwei as Prince of Boling, and Yuan Shuji as Prince of Nanyang, all with the rank of Special Advancement, and removing them from active government.

sentences.zh: 彥範仍賜姓韋氏，令與皇后同屬籍，仍賜雜彩、錦繡、金銀、鞍馬等。

translations.literal: Yanfan was further granted the surname Wei and ordered to share registry affiliation with the empress; he was also given variegated silks, brocades, gold and silver, saddles and horses, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan was even given the surname Wei and enrolled in the same clan register as the empress, along with gifts of colored silks, brocades, gold and silver, saddles, and horses.

sentences.zh: 雖外示優崇，而實奪其權也。

translations.literal: Although outwardly showing favor and elevation, in reality their power was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly they were honored; in truth their power was stripped away.

sentences.zh: 易州刺史趙履溫者，即彥範之妻兄也。

translations.literal: Yi Prefecture prefect Zhao Lüwen was Yanfan's wife's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lüwen, prefect of Yi, was the elder brother of Yanfan's wife.

sentences.zh: 彥範誅易之後，奏言先與履溫共謀其事，於是召拜司農少卿。

translations.literal: After Yanfan executed Yizhi, he memorialized that he had earlier plotted the affair together with Lüwen; Lüwen was therefore summoned and appointed vice minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanfan killed Yizhi, he reported that he had plotted the coup with Lüwen from the start, and Lüwen was summoned and made vice minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 履溫德之，乃以二婢遺彥範。

translations.literal: Lüwen was grateful to him and therefore presented two maidservants to Yanfan.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful, Lüwen gave Yanfan two maidservants.

sentences.zh: 及彥範罷知政事，履溫又協奪其婢，大為時論所譏。

translations.literal: When Yanfan ceased participation in government, Lüwen again forcibly seized back his maidservants, and was greatly ridiculed in contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanfan was removed from office, Lüwen forcibly took the maidservants back, to widespread public scorn.

sentences.zh: 尋出為洺州刺史，轉濠州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as prefect of Ming Prefecture, then transferred to prefect of Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as prefect of Ming, then transferred to prefect of Hao.

sentences.zh: 二年，光祿卿、駙馬都尉王同皎以武三思與韋氏奸通，潛謀誅之。

translations.literal: In the second year, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Commandant of Cavalry Wang Tongjiao, because Wu Sansi had illicit relations with the Wei clan, secretly plotted to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Grand Master Wang Tongjiao, who was also Commandant of Cavalry by marriage to the throne, learned of Wu Sansi's affair with the Wei clan and secretly plotted to kill him.

sentences.zh: 事泄，為三思誣構，言同皎將廢皇后韋氏，彥範等通知其情。

translations.literal: When the affair leaked, Sansi framed him, saying Tongjiao was about to depose Empress Wei and that Yanfan and the others had informed him of the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, Sansi framed him, claiming Tongjiao meant to depose Empress Wei and that Yanfan and his allies had tipped him off.

sentences.zh: 乃貶彥範為瀧州司馬、敬暉崖州司馬、袁恕己竇州司馬、崔玄暐白州司馬、張柬之新州司馬，並仍令長任，勳封並削。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yanfan was demoted to military adjutant of Long Prefecture, Jing Hui to military adjutant of Ya Prefecture, Yuan Shuji to military adjutant of Dou Prefecture, Cui Xuanwei to military adjutant of Bai Prefecture, and Zhang Jianzhi to military adjutant of Xin Prefecture; all were ordered to serve for life, and their merit ranks and fiefs were all stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan was demoted to military adjutant of Long, Jing Hui to adjutant of Ya, Yuan Shuji to adjutant of Dou, Cui Xuanwei to adjutant of Bai, and Zhang Jianzhi to adjutant of Xin; all were ordered to remain in exile for life, and their honors and fiefs were revoked.

sentences.zh: 彥範仍復其本姓桓氏。

translations.literal: Yanfan was further restored to his original surname Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan was also restored to his original surname, Huan.

sentences.zh: 是歲秋，武三思又陰令人疏皇后穢行，榜於天津橋，請加廢黜。

translations.literal: That autumn Wu Sansi again secretly had someone submit a memorial on the empress's licentious conduct, posted it at the Tianjin Bridge, and requested her further deposition.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Wu Sansi secretly had a memorial on the empress's misconduct posted at the Tianjin Bridge, calling for her deposition.

sentences.zh: 中宗聞之怒，命御史大夫李承嘉推求其人。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong heard of it he was angry and ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia to investigate and seek out the person.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was furious and ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia to find who was responsible.

sentences.zh: 承嘉希三思旨，奏言：“彥範與敬暉、張柬之、袁恕己、崔玄暐等教人密為此榜。

translations.literal: Chengjia, hoping to please Sansi's intent, memorialized, saying, "Yanfan, together with Jing Hui, Zhang Jianzhi, Yuan Shuji, Cui Xuanwei, and others had someone secretly make this placard."
translations.idiomatic: Chengjia, eager to please Sansi, reported that Yanfan, Jing Hui, Zhang Jianzhi, Yuan Shuji, Cui Xuanwei, and others had someone post the placard in secret.

sentences.zh: 雖托廢後為名，實有危君之計，請加族滅。

translations.literal: Although they took deposing the empress as their pretext, in reality they had a plan endangering the ruler—I request that their clans be exterminated as well.
translations.idiomatic: Though they used deposing the empress as a pretext, they truly meant to endanger the sovereign; I ask that their entire clans be destroyed.

sentences.zh: ”製依承嘉所奏。

translations.literal: " An edict followed Chengjia's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict approved Chengjia's report.

sentences.zh: 大理丞李朝隱執奏云：“敬暉等既未經鞫問，不可即肆誅夷。

translations.literal: Assistant chief justice Li Chaoyin firmly memorialized, saying, "Jing Hui and the others have not yet undergone interrogation; they cannot immediately be put to death and exterminated."
translations.idiomatic: Assistant chief justice Li Chaoyin objected, saying, "Jing Hui and the others have not even been questioned; they cannot be executed out of hand."

sentences.zh: 請差御史按罪，待至，準法處分。

translations.literal: I request that investigating censors be dispatched to examine their crimes; when they arrive, let punishment be applied according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Send investigating censors to establish their guilt, and when they arrive, punish them according to law.

sentences.zh: ”大理卿裴談奏云：“敬暉等隻合據敕斷罪，不可別俟推鞫，請並處斬籍沒。

translations.literal: " Chief justice Pei Tan memorialized, saying, "Jing Hui and the others should simply be judged guilty according to the edict; one cannot separately await further interrogation—I request that all be executed and their registers confiscated."
translations.idiomatic: " Chief justice Pei Tan argued that Jing Hui and the others should be condemned by edict alone, without further trial, and asked that all be executed and their property confiscated.

sentences.zh: ”中宗納其議，仍以彥範等五人嚐賜鐵券，許以不死，乃長流彥範於州，敬暉於崖州，張柬之於瀧州，袁恕己於環州，崔玄暐於古州，並終身禁錮，子弟年十六已上者亦配流嶺外。

translations.literal: " Zhongzong accepted his proposal, but because Yanfan and the other five men had once been granted iron tallies promising they would not die, they were instead exiled for life: Yanfan to Feng Prefecture, Jing Hui to Ya Prefecture, Zhang Jianzhi to Long Prefecture, Yuan Shuji to Huan Prefecture, and Cui Xuanwei to Gu Prefecture, all under lifelong confinement; sons and younger brothers aged sixteen and above were also banished beyond the Ling ranges.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongzong accepted Pei's view, but because the five men had once been given iron tallies sparing their lives, they were exiled instead: Yanfan to Feng, Jing Hui to Ya, Zhang Jianzhi to Long, Yuan Shuji to Huan, and Cui Xuanwei to Gu, all for life under guard; sons and brothers sixteen or older were also sent beyond the mountains.

sentences.zh: 擢授承嘉金紫光祿大夫，進封襄武郡公。

translations.literal: Chengjia was promoted and appointed Golden-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and advanced to Duke of Xiangwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjia was promoted to Golden-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangwu.

sentences.zh: 韋氏又特賜承嘉彩物五百段、端錦被一張。

translations.literal: The Wei clan also specially granted Chengjia five hundred lengths of colored goods and one brocade quilt of fine weave.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei also gave Chengjia five hundred lengths of colored silks and a brocade coverlet.

sentences.zh: 擢拜裴談為刑部尚書，左貶李朝隱為聞喜令。

translations.literal: Pei Tan was promoted and appointed Minister of Justice; Li Chaoyin was demoted to magistrate of Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Tan was made Minister of Justice; Li Chaoyin was demoted to magistrate of Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 三思俄又諷節湣太子抗表請夷彥範等三族。

translations.literal: Before long Sansi again prompted the Heir Apparent of Jiemin to submit a defiant memorial requesting the extermination of the three clans of Yanfan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Sansi induced the Heir Apparent of Jiemin to memorialize demanding the extermination of Yanfan's clan and those of his allies.

sentences.zh: 中宗以既有前命，不依其請。

translations.literal: Zhongzong, because there was already a prior command, did not follow his request.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong, citing his earlier promise, refused the request.

sentences.zh: 三思猶慮彥範等重被進用，又納中書舍人崔湜之計，特令湜姨兄嘉州司馬周利貞攝右台侍御史，就嶺外並矯製殺之。

translations.literal: Sansi still feared that Yanfan and the others might again be employed, and also adopted the plan of Secretariat Drafting Officer Cui Shi, specially ordering Shi's maternal cousin, Jia Prefecture military adjutant Zhou Lizhen, to act as Right Terrace attendant censor and go beyond the Ling ranges to kill them all by forged edict.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi still feared Yanfan and his allies might return to power, so he took the advice of drafting officer Cui Shi and sent Shi's cousin Zhou Lizhen, military adjutant of Jia, as acting attendant censor of the Right Terrace to the south, where he forged edicts and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 彥範赴流所，行至貴州，利貞遇之於途，乃令左右執縛，曳於竹槎之上，肉盡至骨，然後杖殺，時年五十四。

translations.literal: Yanfan went to his place of exile; when he reached Gui Prefecture, Lizhen met him on the road, ordered his attendants to seize and bind him, dragged him over a bamboo raft until the flesh was worn away to the bone, then beat him to death with staves; he was fifty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan was on his way to exile when he reached Gui Prefecture; Lizhen met him on the road, had him seized and bound, dragged him over a bamboo raft until his flesh was worn to the bone, then clubbed him to death; he was fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，延和元年，並追復其官爵，仍特還其子孫實封二百戶。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, in the first year of Yanhe, all their offices and titles were posthumously restored, and two hundred households of actual fief were specially returned to their sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong came to the throne, in the first year of Yanhe their offices and titles were posthumously restored, and two hundred households of fief were returned to their descendants.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，開元六年，詔曰：“ 皇輿肇建必有輔佐之臣；

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, in the sixth year of Kaiyuan an edict said, "When the imperial carriage is first established there must be assisting ministers;"
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, in the sixth year of Kaiyuan an edict declared, "When the imperial house is first founded, there must be ministers to assist it;"

sentences.zh: 天步多艱，爰仗經綸之業。

translations.literal: when Heaven's steps are many and hard, one relies upon the work of ordering the realm.
translations.idiomatic: when the times are perilous, one must rely on those who can order the realm.

sentences.zh: 故侍中、譙國公桓彥範，侍中、平陽郡公敬暉，中書令兼吏部尚書、漢陽郡公張柬之，特進、博陵郡公崔玄暐，中書令、南陽郡公袁恕己等，並德惟神降，材與運生，道協台嶽，名書讖緯。

translations.literal: Therefore the late Attendant-in-Chief and Duke of Qiao Huan Yanfan, Attendant-in-Chief and Duke of Pingyang Jing Hui, Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Minister of Personnel and Duke of Hanyang Zhang Jianzhi, Special Advancement and Duke of Boling Cui Xuanwei, Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Nanyang Yuan Shuji, and the others—all had virtue as if sent down by the spirits, talent born with the age, the Way in harmony with the terrace and peak, and names written in prognostic texts.
translations.idiomatic: The late Attendant-in-Chief Huan Yanfan, Duke of Qiao; Attendant-in-Chief Jing Hui, Duke of Pingyang; Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Personnel Zhang Jianzhi, Duke of Hanyang; Cui Xuanwei, Duke of Boling; Director of the Secretariat Yuan Shuji, Duke of Nanyang; and the others—all seemed heaven-sent in virtue, born for their age in talent, aligned with the pillars of state, and named in the books of prophecy.

sentences.zh: 寅亮帝載，勤勞王家，參復禹之元謀，奉升唐之景命。

translations.literal: They assisted and brightened the imperial burden, toiled for the royal house, took part in restoring Yu's primal stratagem, and upheld the splendid mandate in raising Tang.
translations.idiomatic: They assisted the throne, labored for the royal house, helped restore the primal design of Yu, and upheld the splendid mandate in raising the Tang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 雖殂謝既久，而勳烈益彰，撫彝鼎以念功，想旂常而增感。

translations.literal: Although they have long since died, their meritorious deeds shine ever brighter; stroking the ritual vessels one recalls their achievements, thinking of the banners in the ancestral hall one's feeling grows.
translations.idiomatic: Though they died long ago, their achievements shine ever brighter; touching the ritual vessels one recalls their service, and thinking of the banners in the ancestral hall one's gratitude deepens.

sentences.zh: 緬遵故實，用表徽懿，俾列在清廟，登於明堂，克申從祀之儀，式茂疇庸之典。

translations.literal: Following distant precedent, to display their fine virtue, let them be arrayed in the Clear Temple and ascend the Bright Hall, fully performing the rites of attendant sacrifice and richly fulfilling the canon of rewarding merit.
translations.idiomatic: Following ancient precedent to display their excellence, let them be enshrined in the Clear Temple and honored in the Bright Hall, that the rites of attendant sacrifice may be fulfilled and the canon of rewarding merit richly observed.

sentences.zh: 並可配享中宗孝和皇帝廟庭，其子北鹹加收擢。

translations.literal: All may receive attendant sacrifice in the temple court of Emperor Xiaozong Xiaohé Zhongzong; their sons all are to receive additional promotion.
translations.idiomatic: All are to share sacrifice in Zhongzong's temple, and their sons are to receive further promotion.

sentences.zh: ”建中元年，重贈司徒。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Jianzhong he was again posthumously given the title Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first year of Jianzhong he was posthumously made Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 初，暉與彥範等誅張易之兄弟也，洛州長史薛季昶謂暉曰：“二凶雖除，產、祿猶在。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hui and Yanfan and the others executed the Zhang Yizhi brothers, Luozhou chief administrator Xue Jichang said to Hui, "Although the two villains are removed, Chan and Lu still remain."
translations.idiomatic: When Hui and Yanfan killed the Zhang brothers, Luozhou chief administrator Xue Jichang told Hui, "The two villains are gone, but Chan and Lu still live."

sentences.zh: 請因兵勢誅武三思之屬，匡正王室，以安天下。

translations.literal: I request that while military momentum holds, the Wu Sansi faction be executed, the royal house set right, and all under Heaven pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Use the army's momentum to destroy Wu Sansi and his faction, set the royal house right, and secure the realm.

sentences.zh: ”暉與張柬之屢陳不可，乃止。

translations.literal: " Hui and Zhang Jianzhi repeatedly stated it could not be done, and so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui and Zhang Jianzhi repeatedly said it could not be done, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 季昶歎曰：“吾不知死所矣。

translations.literal: Jichang sighed and said, "I do not know where I shall die."
translations.idiomatic: Jichang sighed, "I no longer know where I shall meet my end."

sentences.zh: ”翌日，三思因韋後之助，潛入宮中，內行相事，反易國政，為天下所患，時議以此歸咎於暉。

translations.literal: " The next day, with Empress Wei's help, Sansi secretly entered the palace, conducted ministerial affairs within, reversed and altered state government, and became the affliction of all under Heaven; contemporary opinion blamed Hui for this.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day, with Empress Wei's help, Sansi slipped back into the palace, took charge of government from within, reversed state policy, and became a scourge to the realm; public opinion blamed Hui.

sentences.zh: 暉等既失政柄，受製於三思，暉每推床嗟惋，或彈指出血。

translations.literal: When Hui and the others had lost governmental power and fell under Sansi's control, Hui would each time push away his couch and sigh in regret, sometimes flicking his finger until it bled.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hui and his allies lost power and fell under Sansi's control, Hui would push away his couch and sigh in anguish, sometimes flicking his finger until it bled.

sentences.zh: 柬之歎曰：“主上疇昔為英王時，素稱勇烈，吾留諸武，冀自誅鋤耳。

translations.literal: Jianzhi sighed and said, "When the ruler was formerly Prince of Ying, he was known for courage and fierceness; I left the Wu clan in place, hoping he would exterminate them himself."
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi sighed, "When our lord was Prince of Ying, he was famed for courage; I left the Wu clan alive, expecting he would destroy them himself."

sentences.zh: 今事勢已去，知復何道。

translations.literal: Now the situation's momentum is gone—I know not what course remains.
translations.idiomatic: Now the moment has passed—what can be done?

sentences.zh: 三思既深憤惋，以許州司功參軍鄭愔素被暉等廢黜，因令上表陳其罪狀。

translations.literal: Sansi, deeply resentful, used Xu Prefecture merit-records officer Zheng Yin, who had long been demoted by Hui and the others, and had him submit a memorial stating their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi, nursing deep resentment, used Zheng Yin, a records officer of Xu whom Hui and his allies had once demoted, and had him memorialize their crimes.

sentences.zh: 中宗詔曰：“則天大聖皇后，往以憂勞不豫，凶豎弄權。

translations.literal: Zhongzong's edict said, "The Great Sage Empress Wu Zetian, formerly through worry and toil fell ill, and vicious fellows manipulated power."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong's edict read, "The Great Sage Empress Wu, worn down by care and labor, fell ill, and wicked men seized power."

sentences.zh: 暉等因興甲兵，鏟除妖孽，朕錄其勞效，備極寵勞。

translations.literal: Hui and the others therefore raised armed troops and eradicated the demonic spawn; I recorded their meritorious achievement and bestowed the utmost favor and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and his allies raised troops and destroyed these monsters; I recorded their service and lavished favor upon them.

sentences.zh: 自謂勳高一時，遂欲權傾四海，擅作威福，輕侮國章，悖道棄義，莫斯之甚。

translations.literal: Thinking their merit highest in the age, they then wished to tilt power over the four seas, arbitrarily wielding authority and favor, lightly insulting the state's regulations, turning from the Way and abandoning righteousness—nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking their merit unmatched, they sought to dominate the realm, wielding power arbitrarily, scorning the laws of state, and abandoning righteousness—nothing could be worse.

sentences.zh: 然收其薄效，猶為隱忍，錫其郡王之重，優以特進之榮。

translations.literal: Yet gathering their slight achievement, I still bore with them in forbearance, bestowing the weight of princedom and honoring them with the glory of Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for their slight service I still showed forbearance, ennobling them as princes and honoring them with the rank of Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 不謂溪壑之誌，殊難盈滿，既失大權，多懷怨望。

translations.literal: I did not expect that the ambition of ravines and gullies is especially hard to fill; having lost great power, they harbored much resentment.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect their greed to be so insatiable; stripped of power, they nursed deep resentment.

sentences.zh: 乃與王同皎窺覘內禁，潛相謀結，更欲權兵絳闕，圖廢椒宮，險跡醜辭，驚視駭聽。

translations.literal: They then joined Wang Tongjiao in spying on the inner forbidden precinct, secretly plotting together, again wishing to seize troops at the crimson gate, plotting to depose the pepper palace—dangerous tracks and ugly words that startled the eye and shocked the ear.
translations.idiomatic: They joined Wang Tongjiao in spying on the inner palace, plotting in secret to seize troops at the capital gates and depose the empress—deeds and words so vile as to shock all who heard them.

sentences.zh: 屬以帝圖伊始，務靜狴牢，所以久為含容，未能暴諸遐邇。

translations.literal: Since the imperial design had just begun and the task was to quiet the prisons, therefore for long I bore with them and could not expose it far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Because the dynasty had only just been restored and peace was the priority, I long bore with them and did not expose their crimes to the world.

sentences.zh: 自同皎伏法，釁跡彌彰，倘若無其發明，何以懲茲悖亂？

translations.literal: Since Tongjiao submitted to the law, the traces of offense shine ever clearer; if there were not this disclosure, how could such rebellious disorder be punished?
translations.idiomatic: Since Tongjiao was executed, their guilt has become ever clearer; without this exposure, how could such treason be punished?

sentences.zh: 跡其巨逆，合置嚴誅。

translations.literal: Tracing their great rebellion, they ought to receive severe execution.
translations.idiomatic: Given their great treason, they deserve severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 緣其昔立微功，所以特從寬宥，咸宜貶降，出佐遐藩。

translations.literal: Because they once established slight merit, therefore I specially follow lenient pardon: all should be demoted and sent out to assist distant border prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Because they once rendered slight service, I show special leniency: all are to be demoted and sent to distant prefectures.

sentences.zh: 暉可崖州司馬，柬之可新州司馬，恕己可竇州司馬，玄暐可白州司馬，並員外置。

translations.literal: Hui may be Ya Prefecture military adjutant, Jianzhi Xin Prefecture military adjutant, Shuji Dou Prefecture military adjutant, Xuanwei Bai Prefecture military adjutant—all appointed as supernumerary.
translations.idiomatic: Hui is demoted to military adjutant of Ya, Jianzhi to adjutant of Xin, Shuji to adjutant of Dou, and Xuanwei to adjutant of Bai—all as supernumerary appointments.

sentences.zh: ”暉到崖州，竟為周利貞所殺。

translations.literal: " When Hui reached Ya Prefecture, he was in the end killed by Zhou Lizhen.
translations.idiomatic: " When Hui reached Ya Prefecture, Zhou Lizhen killed him.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，追復五王官爵，贈暉秦州都督，諡曰肅湣。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, the five princes' offices and titles were posthumously restored; Hui was given Qin Prefecture regional inspector in gift, with posthumous title Solemn and Mournful.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong came to the throne, the five princes' honors were restored; Hui was posthumously made regional inspector of Qin, with the temple name Solemn and Mournful.

sentences.zh: 建中初，重贈太尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong he was again posthumously given Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong he was posthumously made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 曾孫元膺，開成三年，自試太子通事舍人為河南縣丞。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Yuanying, in the third year of Kaicheng, rose from probationary Crown Prince communications officer to assistant magistrate of Henan county.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Yuanying, in the third year of Kaicheng, advanced from probationary communications officer to the Crown Prince to assistant magistrate of Henan.

sentences.zh: 崔玄暐，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Cui Xuanwei was a native of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuanwei came from Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 父行謹，為胡蘇令。

translations.literal: His father Xingjin was magistrate of Husu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xingjin served as magistrate of Husu.

sentences.zh: 本名曄，以字下體有則天祖諱，乃改為玄暐。

translations.literal: His original name was Ye; because the lower part of the character contained the taboo name of Wu Zetian's ancestor, he changed it to Xuanwei.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Ye; because part of the character violated the taboo on Empress Wu's ancestral name, he changed it to Xuanwei.

sentences.zh: 少有學行，深為叔父秘書監行功所器重。

translations.literal: In youth he had learning and conduct, and was deeply valued by his uncle, Director of the Secretariat Xinggong.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was learned and upright, and his uncle, Director of the Secretariat Xinggong, held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 龍朔中，舉明經，累補庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: During Longshuo he was nominated in the Mingjing examination and was repeatedly appointed to vice director of the stores bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During Longshuo he passed the Mingjing examination and rose to vice director of the stores bureau.

sentences.zh: 其母盧氏嚐誡之曰：“吾見姨兄屯田郎中辛玄馭云：‘兒子從宦者，有人來雲貧乏不能存，此是好消息。

translations.literal: His mother, the Lady Lu, once admonished him, saying, "I heard my cousin, Director of Agriculture Xin Xuanyu, say: 'When a son enters official service, if someone reports he is poor and cannot support himself, that is good news.'"
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Lu, once warned him, "I heard my cousin Xin Xuanyu, director of agriculture, say: 'When a son enters office, word that he is poor and struggling to get by is good news.'"

sentences.zh: 若聞貲貨充足，衣馬輕肥，此惡消息。

translations.literal: If one hears that goods and wealth are ample, clothes and horses light and fat—that is bad news.'"
translations.idiomatic: If one hears he is flush with goods, well dressed, and riding fine horses—that is bad news.'"

sentences.zh: ’吾常重此言，以為確論。

translations.literal: ' I have always valued these words and taken them as settled doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: ' I have always treasured these words as sound doctrine.

sentences.zh: 比見親表中仕宦者，多將錢物上其父母，父母但知喜悅，竟不問此物從何而來。

translations.literal: Recently I have seen among relatives and clan members in office that many bring money and goods to present to their parents; the parents only know joy and never ask whence these things came.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I have seen many relatives in office send money and goods to their parents; the parents rejoice and never ask where the gifts came from.

sentences.zh: 必是祿俸餘資，誠亦善事。

translations.literal: If it must be surplus from salary and stipend, that is truly also a good matter.
translations.idiomatic: If it truly comes from surplus salary, that is indeed a good thing.

sentences.zh: 如其非理所得，此與盜賊何別？

translations.literal: If it is obtained unreasonably, how does this differ from thieves and robbers?
translations.idiomatic: If it was gained improperly, how is that different from theft?

sentences.zh: 縱無大咎，獨不內愧於心？

translations.literal: Even if there is no great fault, does one not feel inner shame in the heart?
translations.idiomatic: Even if no great crime is committed, does one feel no shame within?

sentences.zh: 孟母不受魚鮓之饋，蓋為此也。

translations.literal: Mencius's mother did not accept the gift of fish and salted meat—surely it was for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius's mother refused the gift of fish and salted meat for just this reason.

sentences.zh: 汝今坐食祿俸，榮幸已多，若其不能忠清，何以戴天履地？

translations.literal: You now sit and eat salary and stipend; honor and fortune are already many—if you cannot be loyal and pure, how can you bear up Heaven and tread Earth?
translations.idiomatic: You now live on official salary and enjoy great honor; if you cannot remain loyal and upright, how can you face Heaven and earth?

sentences.zh: 孔子云：‘雖日殺三性之養，猶為不孝。

translations.literal: Confucius said, 'Even if one daily slaughters the three sacrificial animals for nourishment, it is still unfilial.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Even if one sacrifices three animals every day for one's parents, it is still unfilial."

sentences.zh: ’又曰：‘父母惟其疾之憂。

translations.literal: ' He also said, 'Parents have concern only for their children's illness.'
translations.idiomatic: ' He also said, 'Parents care only that their children be free of illness.'

sentences.zh: ’持宜修身潔已，勿累吾此意也。

translations.literal: ' You should cultivate the self and keep the person pure, and not burden my intent in this.'"
translations.idiomatic: ' Keep your conduct pure and do not betray what I mean by this.'"

sentences.zh: ”玄暐遵奉母氏教誡，以清謹見稱。

translations.literal: " Xuanwei followed his mother's teachings and was known for purity and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanwei followed his mother's counsel and was famed for integrity and discretion.

sentences.zh: 尋授天宮郎中，遷鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed director of the heaven bureau, then transferred to Phoenix Pavilion drafting officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made director of the heaven bureau, then promoted to drafting officer of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 則天季年，宋璟劾奏張昌宗謀為不軌，玄暐亦屢有讜言，則天乃令法司正斷其罪。

translations.literal: In the late years of Wu Zetian, Song Jing impeached Zhang Changzong for plotting irregular conduct; Xuanwei also repeatedly offered forthright counsel, and Wu Zetian then ordered the legal offices to judge his crime correctly.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Empress Wu's reign, Song Jing impeached Zhang Changzong for treasonous plotting; Xuanwei also spoke out repeatedly, and the empress ordered the courts to judge the case properly.

sentences.zh: 玄暐弟升時為司刑少卿，又請置以大辟。

translations.literal: Xuanwei's younger brother Sheng was then vice minister of justice and also requested that the great execution be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwei's brother Sheng, then vice minister of justice, also asked that the death penalty be imposed.

sentences.zh: 其兄弟守正如此。

translations.literal: The brothers upheld rectitude to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were so steadfast in righteousness.

sentences.zh: 是時，則天不豫，宰相不得召見者累月。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Zetian was ill, and the chief ministers could not be summoned for audience for many months.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Wu was ill, and the chief ministers went months without audience.

sentences.zh: 及疾少間，玄暐奏言：“皇太子、相王仁明孝友，足可親侍湯藥。

translations.literal: When her illness eased slightly, Xuanwei memorialized, saying, "The Crown Prince and the Prince of Xiang are benevolent, bright, filial, and friendly—fully able to attend personally to medicines."
translations.idiomatic: When her illness eased slightly, Xuanwei memorialized, "The Crown Prince and the Prince of Xiang are benevolent, filial, and fit to attend you with medicine in person."

sentences.zh: 宮禁事重，伏願不令異姓出入。

translations.literal: Palace prohibitions are weighty matters; I humbly wish that persons of other surnames not be allowed to enter and leave.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace is a grave matter; I beg that no outsiders of other surnames be allowed in.

sentences.zh: ”則天曰：“深領卿厚意。

translations.literal: " Wu Zetian said, "I deeply receive your generous intent."
translations.idiomatic: " The empress said, "I am deeply grateful for your thoughtful concern."

sentences.zh: ”尋以預誅張易之功，擢拜中書令，封博陵郡公。

translations.literal: " Soon, for his merit in the prior execution of Zhang Yizhi, he was promoted and appointed Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Boling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon, for his part in killing Zhang Yizhi, he was made Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Boling.

sentences.zh: 中宗將授方術人鄭普思為秘書監，玄暐切諫，竟不納。

translations.literal: Zhongzong was about to appoint the technician Zheng Pusi Director of the Secretariat; Xuanwei remonstrated sharply, but in the end it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was about to make the occultist Zheng Pusi Director of the Secretariat; Xuanwei protested strongly, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 尋進爵為王，賜實封四百戶，檢校益州大都督府長史，兼知都督事。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced in rank to prince, granted four hundred households of actual fief, made acting chief administrator of the Yi metropolitan area, and concurrently directed regional inspector affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to prince, given a fief of four hundred households, made acting chief administrator of Yi, and placed in charge of regional military affairs.

sentences.zh: 其後被累貶，授白州司馬，在道病卒。

translations.literal: Afterward he was implicated and demoted, appointed military adjutant of Bai Prefecture, and died of illness on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He was later implicated in the purge, demoted to military adjutant of Bai, and died of illness on the way to exile.

sentences.zh: 建中初，贈太子太師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong he was posthumously given Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong he was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 玄暐與弟升甚相友愛。

translations.literal: Xuanwei and his younger brother Sheng were very affectionate toward each other.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwei and his brother Sheng were deeply devoted to each other.

sentences.zh: 諸子弟孤貧者，多躬自撫養教授，頗為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Among the younger clansmen who were orphaned and poor, many he personally reared and instructed, and he was much praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He personally raised and taught many orphaned and poor younger kinsmen, winning wide praise in his day.

sentences.zh: 升，官至尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Sheng rose in office to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng rose to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 玄暐少時頗屬詩賦，晚年以為非己所長，乃不復構思，唯篤誌經籍，述作為事。

translations.literal: In youth Xuanwei often composed poetry and fu; in his later years he thought these were not his strengths, and so no longer conceived them, devoting himself solely to the classics and taking authorship as his task.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Xuanwei wrote poetry and rhapsodies, but in later years he decided they were not his strength and gave them up, devoting himself to the classics and scholarly writing.

sentences.zh: 所撰《行己要範》十卷、《友義傳》十卷、《義士傳》十五卷、訓注《文館辭林策》二十卷，並行於代。

translations.literal: His compositions included Essentials of Conduct in ten scrolls, Record of Friendship in ten scrolls, Record of Men of Righteousness in fifteen scrolls, and Annotated Examinations of the Forest of Literary Phrases of the Literary Hall in twenty scrolls—all circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Essentials of Conduct in ten scrolls, Record of Friendship in ten scrolls, Record of Men of Righteousness in fifteen scrolls, and Annotated Examinations of the Forest of Literary Phrases in twenty scrolls—all widely read in his time.

sentences.zh: 子璩，頗以文學知名，官曆中書舍人、禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Qu was fairly known for literary learning and served as Secretariat drafting officer and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qu was known for literary talent and served as drafting officer of the Secretariat and Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 璩子渙，自有傳。

translations.literal: Qu's son Huan has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Qu's son Huan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 曾孫郢，開成三年，自商州防禦判官兼殿中侍御史，入為監察御史。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Ying, in the third year of Kaicheng, rose from Shang Prefecture defense staff judge and concurrent attendant censor within the palace to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Ying, in the third year of Kaicheng, advanced from staff judge on the Shang defense command and attendant censor within the palace to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 張柬之，字孟將，襄州襄陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianzhi, style name Mengjiang, was a native of Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianzhi, courtesy name Mengjiang, came from Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少補太學生，涉獵經史，尤好《三禮》，國子祭酒令狐德棻甚重之。

translations.literal: In youth he entered the Imperial Academy as a student, ranged through the classics and histories, especially loved the Three Rites, and was greatly valued by Libationer of the Directorate of Education Linghu Defen.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he entered the Imperial Academy, studied the classics and histories, especially favored the Three Rites, and was highly regarded by Libationer Linghu Defen.

sentences.zh: 進士擢第，累補青城丞。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly appointed assistant magistrate of Qingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served successively as assistant magistrate of Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，以賢良征試，同時策者千餘人，柬之獨為當時第一，擢拜監察御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang he was summoned for the worthy and good examination; of more than a thousand who answered the policy questions at the same time, Jianzhi alone was first in his time and was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchang he took the worthy-and-good examination; among more than a thousand candidates he alone ranked first and was made investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 聖曆初，累遷鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengli he was repeatedly promoted to Phoenix Pavilion drafting officer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shengli era he rose to drafting officer of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 時弘文館直學士王元感著論云：“三年之喪，合三十六月。

translations.literal: At that time Hongwen Hall direct academician Wang Yuangan wrote a treatise saying, "The three-year mourning totals thirty-six months."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Yuangan, direct academician of the Hongwen Hall, wrote a treatise arguing that the three-year mourning period totals thirty-six months.

sentences.zh: ”柬之著論駁之曰：

translations.literal: " Jianzhi wrote a treatise refuting him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: " Jianzhi wrote a rebuttal, stating:

sentences.zh: 三年之喪，二十五月，不刊之典也。

translations.literal: The three-year mourning is twenty-five months—an immutable canon.
translations.idiomatic: The three-year mourning is twenty-five months—an immutable standard.

sentences.zh: 謹案《春秋》：“魯僖公三十三年十二月乙巳，公薨。

translations.literal: I respectfully examine the Spring and Autumn Annals: "In the thirty-third year of Duke Xi of Lu, in the twelfth month on the day yisi, the duke died."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Spring and Autumn Annals: "In the thirty-third year of Duke Xi of Lu, on the day yisi of the twelfth month, the duke died."

sentences.zh: ”“文公二年冬，公子遂如齊納幣。

translations.literal: " "In the second year of Duke Wen, in winter, the duke's son Sui went to Qi to present betrothal gifts."
translations.idiomatic: " "In the second year of Duke Wen, in winter, the duke's son Sui went to Qi to present betrothal gifts."

sentences.zh: ”《左傳》曰“禮也。

translations.literal: " The Zuo Commentary says, "It was according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: " The Zuo Commentary says, "This was ritual propriety."

sentences.zh: ”杜預注云：“僖公喪終此年十一月，納幣在十二月。

translations.literal: " Du Yu's commentary says, "Duke Xi's mourning ended in the eleventh month of this year; the betrothal gifts were presented in the twelfth month."
translations.idiomatic: " Du Yu comments, "Duke Xi's mourning ended in the eleventh month of that year; the betrothal gifts were presented in the twelfth."

sentences.zh: 士婚禮，納采納徵，皆有玄纁束帛，諸侯則謂之納幣。

translations.literal: In the marriage rites of a gentleman, presenting the proposal and presenting the betrothal gift both have dark and light silk with bundled cloth; for feudal lords this is called presenting betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In a gentleman's wedding rites, the proposal and betrothal gifts both include dark and light silks bound as offerings; for feudal lords this is called presenting betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 蓋公為太子，已行婚禮。

translations.literal: The duke, as heir apparent, had already performed the marriage rites.
translations.idiomatic: The duke, as crown prince, had already performed the marriage rites.

sentences.zh: ”故《傳》稱禮也。

translations.literal: " Therefore the Commentary calls it ritual.
translations.idiomatic: " Hence the Commentary calls it proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 《公羊傳》曰：“ 納幣不書，此何以書？

translations.literal: The Gongyang Commentary says, "Presenting betrothal gifts is not recorded—why is this recorded?"
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang Commentary asks, "Betrothal gifts are not normally recorded—why is this recorded?"

sentences.zh: 譏喪娶。

translations.literal: To censure marrying during mourning.
translations.idiomatic: To condemn marriage during mourning.

sentences.zh: 在三年之外何以譏？

translations.literal: If outside the three years, why censure?
translations.idiomatic: If it were outside the three-year period, why censure it?

sentences.zh: 三年之內不圖婚。

translations.literal: Within the three years one does not contemplate marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Within the three-year mourning one must not contemplate marriage.

sentences.zh: ”何休注云：“僖公以十二月薨，至此冬未滿二十五月，納采、問名、納吉，皆在三年之內，故譏。

translations.literal: " He Xiu's commentary says, "Duke Xi died in the twelfth month; by this winter twenty-five months had not yet been filled; presenting the proposal, inquiring the name, and presenting the auspicious confirmation were all within the three years—therefore censure."
translations.idiomatic: " He Xiu comments, "Duke Xi died in the twelfth month; by this winter twenty-five months had not passed; the proposal, name inquiry, and auspicious confirmation all fell within the mourning period—hence the censure."

sentences.zh: ”何休以公十二月薨，至此冬十二月才二十四月，非二十五月，是未三年而圖婚也。

translations.literal: " He Xiu, taking that the duke died in the twelfth month and that by this winter's twelfth month there were only twenty-four months—not twenty-five months—holds that the three years had not been completed and marriage was contemplated.
translations.idiomatic: " He Xiu, reckoning from the duke's death in the twelfth month to this winter's twelfth month as only twenty-four months—not twenty-five—concludes that the mourning had not ended and marriage was premature.

sentences.zh: 按《經》書“十二月乙巳公薨”，杜預以《長曆》推乙巳是十一月十二日，非十二月，書十二月，是《經》誤。

translations.literal: Examining the Classic's record "in the twelfth month on yisi the duke died," Du Yu, using the Long Calendar, calculated that yisi was the twelfth day of the eleventh month, not the twelfth month; recording the twelfth month is an error in the Classic.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic records "on yisi of the twelfth month the duke died," but Du Yu, using the Long Calendar, calculated that yisi fell on the twelfth day of the eleventh month; the twelfth-month date in the Classic is an error.

sentences.zh: “文公元年四月，葬我君僖公”，《傳》曰，緩也。

translations.literal: "In the first year of Duke Wen, in the fourth month, we buried our lord Duke Xi"; the Commentary says this was delayed.
translations.idiomatic: "In the first year of Duke Wen, in the fourth month, we buried our lord Duke Xi"; the Commentary calls this delayed.

sentences.zh: 諸侯五月而葬，若是十二月薨，即是五月，不得言緩。

translations.literal: Feudal lords are buried in the fifth month; if he died in the twelfth month, this would be the fifth month and one could not call it delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords are buried in the fifth month after death; if he died in the twelfth month, burial in the fourth month of the following year would be on time, not delayed.

sentences.zh: 明知是十一月薨，故注僖公喪終此年，至十二月而滿二十五月，故丘明《傳》曰，禮也。

translations.literal: Knowing clearly that he died in the eleventh month, he therefore notes that Duke Xi's mourning ended within this year, reaching the twelfth month to complete twenty-five months; therefore Qiu Ming's Commentary says this accorded with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Since it is clear Duke Xi died in the eleventh month, Du Yu notes that his mourning ended within that year and was complete at twenty-five months by the twelfth month; hence Qiu Ming's Commentary calls this proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 據此推步，杜之考校，豈公羊之所能逮，況丘明親受《經》於仲尼乎？

translations.literal: Based on this reckoning, Du Yu's textual verification—how could the Gongyang [tradition] reach it, moreover when Qiu Ming personally received the Classic from Confucius?
translations.idiomatic: By this calculation, Du Yu's textual work is beyond what the Gongyang Commentary can match—especially since Qiu Ming received the Classic directly from Confucius.

sentences.zh: 且二《傳》何、杜所爭，唯爭一月，不爭一年。

translations.literal: Moreover, what He Xiu and Du Yu dispute between the two Commentaries is only one month, not a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, He Xiu and Du Yu dispute only one month between the two Commentaries—not an entire year.

sentences.zh: 其二十五月除喪，由來無別。

translations.literal: That mourning ends at twenty-five months has never been disputed.
translations.idiomatic: That mourning ends at twenty-five months has never been in dispute.

sentences.zh: 此則《春秋》三年之喪，二十五月之明驗也。

translations.literal: This is clear proof from the Spring and Autumn Annals that the three-year mourning period lasts twenty-five months.
translations.idiomatic: This is clear proof from the Spring and Autumn Annals that the three-year mourning lasts twenty-five months.

sentences.zh: 《尚書·伊訓》云：“成湯既沒，太甲元年，惟元祀十有二月，伊尹祀於先王，奉嗣王祗見厥祖。

translations.literal: The Book of Documents, "Instructions of Yi," says: "When Cheng Tang had passed, in the first year of Tai Jia, in the twelfth month of the first year, Yi Yin sacrificed to the former kings and presented the heir king reverently to appear before his ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents, "Instructions of Yi," says: "After Cheng Tang died, in the first year of Tai Jia, in the twelfth month of the inaugural year, Yi Yin sacrificed to the former kings and brought the heir king to appear reverently before his ancestor.

sentences.zh: ”孔安國注云：“湯以元年十一月崩。

translations.literal: " Kong Anguo's commentary says: "Tang died in the eleventh month of the first year.
translations.idiomatic: " Kong Anguo comments: "Tang died in the eleventh month of the first year.

sentences.zh: ”據此，則二年十一月小祥，三年十一月大祥。

translations.literal: " Based on this, the lesser memorial would fall in the eleventh month of the second year, and the greater memorial in the eleventh month of the third year.
translations.idiomatic: " From this it follows that the lesser memorial came in the eleventh month of the second year and the greater memorial in the eleventh month of the third year.

sentences.zh: 故《太甲》中篇云：“惟三祀十有二月朔，伊尹以冕服奉嗣王歸於亳。

translations.literal: Therefore the middle section of "Tai Jia" says: "In the twelfth month of the third year, on the new moon, Yi Yin with cap and robes presented the heir king back to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the middle section of "Tai Jia" says: "In the twelfth month of the third year, on the first day of the month, Yi Yin in cap and robes brought the heir king back to Bo.

sentences.zh: ”是十一月大祥，訖十二月朔日，加王冕服吉而歸亳也。

translations.literal: " This is the greater memorial in the eleventh month; from then until the new moon of the twelfth month, the king donned his cap and robes in auspicious fashion and returned to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: " This marks the greater memorial in the eleventh month; by the new moon of the twelfth month the king had put on his cap and robes in auspicious fashion and returned to Bo.

sentences.zh: 是孔言“湯元年十一月”之明驗。

translations.literal: This is clear proof of Kong's statement that "Tang died in the eleventh month of the first year."
translations.idiomatic: This confirms Kong Anguo's claim that Tang died in the eleventh month of the first year.

sentences.zh: 《顧命》云：“四月哉生魄，王不懌”，是四月十六日也。

translations.literal: "Charge to the Chung" says: "On the sixteenth of the fourth month, the king was displeased"—this is the sixteenth day of the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: The "Charge to the Chung" says: "On the sixteenth of the fourth month, the king was displeased"—that is, the sixteenth day of the fourth month.

sentences.zh: “翌日乙丑，王崩”，是十七日也。

translations.literal: "On the next day, yichou, the king died"—this is the seventeenth day.
translations.idiomatic: "On the following day, yichou, the king died"—the seventeenth day.

sentences.zh: “丁卯，命作冊度”，是十九日也。

translations.literal: "On dingmao, he ordered the making of the written charge"—this is the nineteenth day.
translations.idiomatic: "On dingmao, he ordered the written charge to be prepared"—the nineteenth day.

sentences.zh: “越七日癸酉，伯相命士須材”，是四月二十五日也。

translations.literal: "Seven days later on guiyou, the prime minister ordered the officers to prepare the materials"—this is the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: "Seven days later, on guiyou, the prime minister ordered the officers to gather the materials"—the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 則成王崩至康王麻冕黼裳，中間有十月，康王方始見廟。

translations.literal: From King Cheng's death until King Kang appeared in the temple wearing hemp cap and embroidered robe, ten months elapsed before King Kang first appeared at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: From King Cheng's death until King Kang appeared at the ancestral temple in hemp cap and embroidered robe, ten months passed before Kang first entered the temple.

sentences.zh: 則知湯崩在十一月，淹停至殮訖，方始十二月，祗見其祖。

translations.literal: Thus we know Tang died in the eleventh month; the waiting period until encoffining was complete reached only then into the twelfth month, when the heir reverently appeared before his ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: This shows Tang died in the eleventh month; only after the waiting period and encoffining were complete, in the twelfth month, did the heir reverently appear before his ancestor.

sentences.zh: 《顧命》見廟訖，諸侯出廟門俟，《伊訓》言“祗見厥祖，侯甸群後鹹在’，則崩及見廟，殷、周之禮並同。

translations.literal: After the temple visit in "Charge to the Chung" was complete, the feudal lords waited outside the temple gate; "Instructions of Yi" states "reverently appearing before his ancestor, the marquisates, domains, and multitude of nobles were all present"—thus from death until the temple visit, Yin and Zhou ritual were the same.
translations.idiomatic: In "Charge to the Chung," after the temple visit the feudal lords waited outside the gate; "Instructions of Yi" says "reverently appearing before his ancestor, the marquisates, domains, and assembled nobles were all present"—so from death to the temple visit, Yin and Zhou practice was the same.

sentences.zh: 此周因於殷禮，損益可知也。

translations.literal: This shows how Zhou inherited from Yin ritual—what was reduced or augmented can be known.
translations.idiomatic: This shows how Zhou drew on Yin ritual—what was kept, reduced, or added can be seen clearly.

sentences.zh: 不得元年以前，別有一年。

translations.literal: One cannot count a separate year before the first year [of the reign].
translations.idiomatic: One cannot count an extra year before the first year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 此《尚書》三年之喪，二十五月之明驗也。

translations.literal: This is clear proof from the Book of Documents that the three-year mourning lasts twenty-five months.
