translations.idiomatic: This is clear proof from the Book of Documents that the three-year mourning period lasts twenty-five months.

sentences.zh: 《禮記三年問》云：“三年之喪，二十五月而畢，哀痛未盡，思慕未忘，然而服以是斷之者，豈不送死有已，復生有節？

translations.literal: Records of Rites, "Three-Year Inquiry," says: "The three-year mourning, twenty-five months and it is complete—grief and pain not exhausted, longing and remembrance not forgotten, yet mourning garments end here—is it not that sending off the dead has its limit and returning to life has its measure?
translations.idiomatic: The Records of Rites, "Three-Year Inquiry," says: "The three-year mourning ends at twenty-five months. Grief is not yet spent and longing is not yet forgotten, yet mourning dress stops here—is this not because sending off the dead must have its limit and returning to life must have its proper measure?

sentences.zh: ”又《喪服四製》云：“變而從宜，故大祥鼓素琴，告人以終。

translations.literal: " Again, "Four Principles of Mourning Garments" says: "Changing to follow what is fitting, therefore at the great memorial one strikes the plain zither, announcing to others that mourning has ended.
translations.idiomatic: " Again, "Four Principles of Mourning Garments" says: "One changes to follow what is fitting; therefore at the great memorial one strikes the plain zither to tell others that mourning is over.

sentences.zh: ”又《間傳》云：“期而小祥，食菜果。

translations.literal: " Again, "Treatise on Progressive Stages" says: "One cycle and the lesser memorial; one eats vegetables and fruit.
translations.idiomatic: " Again, "Treatise on Progressive Stages" says: "After one full cycle comes the lesser memorial, and one may eat vegetables and fruit.

sentences.zh: 又期而大祥，有醯醬。

translations.literal: Another cycle and the great memorial; there is vinegar and sauce.
translations.idiomatic: After another cycle comes the great memorial, and one may have vinegar and sauce.

sentences.zh: 中月而禫，食酒肉。

translations.literal: In the intervening month comes the sacrificial release of mourning; one eats wine and meat.
translations.idiomatic: In the month between comes the sacrificial release of mourning, and one may eat wine and meat.

sentences.zh: ”又《喪服小記》云：“再期之喪，三年也。

translations.literal: " Again, "Small Record on Mourning Garments" says: "Mourning of two cycles is the three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: " Again, "Small Record on Mourning Garments" says: "Mourning lasting two full cycles is the three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 期之喪，二年也。

translations.literal: Mourning of one cycle is two years.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning of one cycle is two years.

sentences.zh: 九月七月之喪，三時也。

translations.literal: Mourning of nine or seven months is three seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning of nine or seven months spans three seasons.

sentences.zh: 五月之喪，二時也。

translations.literal: Mourning of five months is two seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning of five months spans two seasons.

sentences.zh: 三月之喪，一時也。

translations.literal: Mourning of three months is one season.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning of three months spans one season.

sentences.zh: ”此《禮記》三年之喪，二十五月之明驗也。

translations.literal: " This is clear proof from the Records of Rites that the three-year mourning lasts twenty-five months.
translations.idiomatic: " This is clear proof from the Records of Rites that the three-year mourning period lasts twenty-five months.

sentences.zh: 《儀禮士虞禮》云：“期而小祥。

translations.literal: Rites of Etiquette and Ceremonial, "Officer's Sacrificial Rites," says: "One cycle and the lesser memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Etiquette and Ceremonial, "Officer's Sacrificial Rites," says: "After one cycle comes the lesser memorial.

sentences.zh: 又期而大祥。

translations.literal: Another cycle and the great memorial.
translations.idiomatic: After another cycle comes the great memorial.

sentences.zh: 中月而禫，是月也吉祭。

translations.literal: In the intervening month comes the sacrificial release of mourning; in that month the auspicious sacrifice is performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the month between comes the sacrificial release of mourning, and in that month the auspicious sacrifice is held.

sentences.zh: ”此禮周公所製，則《儀禮》三年之喪，二十五月之明驗也。

translations.literal: " This rite was established by the Duke of Zhou; thus the Rites of Etiquette and Ceremonial's three-year mourning is clear proof of twenty-five months.
translations.idiomatic: " This rite was established by the Duke of Zhou, so the Rites of Etiquette and Ceremonial provides clear proof that the three-year mourning lasts twenty-five months.

sentences.zh: 此四驗者，並禮經正文，或周公所製，或仲尼所述，吾子豈得以《禮記》戴聖所修，輒欲排毀？

translations.literal: These four proofs are all canonical ritual texts—either established by the Duke of Zhou or set forth by Confucius—how can you, sir, because the Records of Rites was compiled by Dai Sheng, rashly wish to reject and destroy them?
translations.idiomatic: These four proofs are all canonical ritual texts—some made by the Duke of Zhou, some set forth by Confucius. How can you, sir, simply because Dai Sheng compiled the Records of Rites, seek to dismiss and tear them down?

sentences.zh: 漢初高堂生傳《禮》，既未周備，宣帝時少傳後蒼因淹中孔壁所得五十六篇著《曲台記》，以授弟子戴德、戴聖、慶溥三人，合以正經及孫卿所述，並相符會。

translations.literal: In early Han, Gaotang Sheng transmitted the Rites, which was not yet complete; in Emperor Xuan's time the junior guardian Hou Cang, using the fifty-six chapters obtained from the Kong wall at Yanzhong, wrote "Record of the Qu Platform" and taught it to his disciples Dai De, Dai Sheng, and Qing Pu; combining it with the orthodox classic and what Sun Qing set forth, all accorded with one another.
translations.idiomatic: In early Han Gaotang Sheng transmitted the Rites, but it was incomplete. Under Emperor Xuan, the junior guardian Hou Cang used the fifty-six chapters found in the Kong wall at Yanzhong to compose the "Record of the Qu Platform" and taught it to his disciples Dai De, Dai Sheng, and Qing Pu. Combined with the orthodox classic and Sun Qing's teachings, everything matched.

sentences.zh: 列於學官，年代已久。

translations.literal: It was listed at the academies, and many years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: It has stood in the official curriculum for many years.

sentences.zh: 今無端構造異論，既無依據，深可歎息。

translations.literal: Now you groundlessly construct heterodox views without any basis—deeply lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Now you invent strange doctrines without basis—a cause for deep regret.

sentences.zh: 其二十五月，先儒考校，唯鄭康成注《儀禮》“中月而禫”，以“中月間一月，自死至禫凡二十七月”。

translations.literal: As for the twenty-five months, among earlier scholars' verification, only Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Rites of Etiquette and Ceremonial, "in the intervening month comes the sacrificial release of mourning," takes "the intervening month as one month between, from death to sacrificial release altogether twenty-seven months."
translations.idiomatic: On the question of twenty-five months, earlier scholars agreed on almost everything; only Zheng Xuan, commenting on the Rites of Etiquette and Ceremonial's phrase "in the intervening month comes the sacrificial release of mourning," counted one month in between and held that from death to sacrificial release was twenty-seven months in all.

sentences.zh: 又解禫云：“言澹澹然平安之意也。

translations.literal: He also explained sacrificial release, saying: "It means the sense of tranquil peace.
translations.idiomatic: He also explained sacrificial release, saying: "It expresses the meaning of calm and peace.

sentences.zh: ”今皆二十七月復常，從鄭議也。

translations.literal: " Now all return to normal at twenty-seven months, following Zheng's view.
translations.idiomatic: " Today everyone returns to normal life at twenty-seven months, following Zheng Xuan's view.

sentences.zh: 逾月入禫，禫既復常，則二十五月為免喪矣。

translations.literal: Entering sacrificial release after a month beyond, once release returns to normal, then twenty-five months is when mourning is ended.
translations.idiomatic: Entering sacrificial release one month later, once that release marks a return to normal life, twenty-five months is when mourning ends.

sentences.zh: 二十五月、二十七月，其議本同。

translations.literal: Twenty-five months and twenty-seven months—their positions are fundamentally the same.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-five-month and twenty-seven-month positions are fundamentally the same.

sentences.zh: 竊以子之於父母喪也，有終身之痛，創巨者日久，痛深者愈遲，豈徒歲月而已乎？

translations.literal: I privately hold that in mourning for one's parents there is lifelong pain—great wounds take long to heal, deep pain heals more slowly—how could it be merely a matter of months and years?
translations.idiomatic: I believe that mourning for one's parents brings lifelong pain. Great wounds take long to heal; the deeper the grief, the slower it fades. How could it be only a matter of months and years?

sentences.zh: 故練而慨然者，蓋悲慕之懷未盡，而踴擗之情已歇；

translations.literal: Therefore at lian one is sighing deeply—because the feelings of grief and longing are not yet exhausted, while the fervor of beating one's breast has already ceased;
translations.idiomatic: That is why at lian one still sighs deeply: grief and longing are not yet spent, but the fierce beating of the breast has already stopped;

sentences.zh: 祥而廓然者，蓋哀傷之痛已除，而孤邈之念更起。

translations.literal: At xiang one is suddenly open—because the pain of sorrow and mourning has been removed, while thoughts of loneliness and distance rise anew.
translations.idiomatic: at xiang one feels suddenly emptied because the sharp pain of mourning has lifted, yet thoughts of loneliness and distance rise anew.

sentences.zh: 此皆情之所致，豈外飾哉。

translations.literal: All these come from genuine emotion—how could they be outer adornment?
translations.idiomatic: All of this comes from genuine feeling—how could it be mere outward show?

sentences.zh: 故《記》曰：三年之喪，義同過隙，先王立其中製，以成文理。

translations.literal: Therefore the Record says: the three-year mourning, its principle is like passing through a crack—the ancient kings established the mean measure to complete the pattern of culture.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Record says: the three-year mourning, in principle, passes like a crack in time; the ancient kings set a middle measure to give culture its proper form.

sentences.zh: 是以祥則縞帶素紕，禫則無所不佩。

translations.literal: Therefore at xiang one wears white sash and plain hem; at sacrificial release one may wear all ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore at xiang one wears a white sash and plain hem; at sacrificial release one may wear every ornament again.

sentences.zh: 今吾子將徇情棄禮，實為乖僻。

translations.literal: Now you, sir, would follow emotion and abandon ritual—this is truly perverse.
translations.idiomatic: Now you would indulge feeling and cast off ritual—a truly perverse course.

sentences.zh: 夫棄縗麻之服，襲錦縠之衣，行道之人，皆不忍也，直為節之以禮，無可奈何。

translations.literal: To cast off hemp mourning garments and put on brocaded silk—travelers on the road could not bear to see it; it is only restrained by ritual, with no alternative.
translations.idiomatic: To cast off coarse hemp mourning dress and put on brocaded silk—any passerby would find it unbearable to watch. Ritual restrains us because there is no other way.

sentences.zh: 故由也不能過製為姊服，鯉也不能過期哭其母。

translations.literal: Therefore Zilu could not exceed the prescribed mourning for his elder sister, and Boyu's son Li could not mourn his mother beyond the stipulated period.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Zilu could not exceed the prescribed mourning for his elder sister, and Boyu's son Li could not mourn his mother past the allotted time.

sentences.zh: 夫豈不懷，懼名教逼己也。

translations.literal: Did they not feel grief? They feared that the norms of civilization would constrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Was it that they felt no grief? No—they feared the constraints of civilization and propriety.

sentences.zh: 若孔、鄭、何、杜之徒，並命代挺生，範模來裔，宮牆積仞，未易可窺。

translations.literal: If Confucius, Zheng, He, Du and such masters, endowed by fate for their generation, models for future descendants—the palace wall piled many ren high—not easily peered over.
translations.idiomatic: Masters such as Confucius, Zheng Xuan, He Xiu, and Du Yu were born for their age and became models for later generations. Their learning stands like a palace wall piled many ren high—not easily looked over.

sentences.zh: 但鑽仰不休，當漸入勝境，詎勞終年矻矻，虛肆莠言？

translations.literal: Only by drilling and looking upward without ceasing should one gradually enter the realm of mastery—why toil year-round in dull labor and vainly spread weeds of words?
translations.idiomatic: Only by drilling and looking upward without ceasing can one gradually reach mastery. Why toil all year in fruitless labor and spread empty weeds of words?

sentences.zh: 請所有掎擿先儒，願且以時消息。

translations.literal: I beg that all your picking at earlier scholars' views may for now rest with the times.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that your attacks on earlier scholars may for now be set aside and allowed to rest.

sentences.zh: 時人以柬之所駁，頗合於禮典。

translations.literal: People of the time considered Jianzhi's refutations largely in accord with ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time felt that Jianzhi's refutations largely accorded with the ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 是歲，突厥默啜表言有女請和親，則天盛意許之，欲令淮陽郡王延秀娶之。

translations.literal: That year, the Turk khan Moqi memorialized that he had a daughter and sought marriage alliance; Wu Zetian gladly agreed and intended to have the Prince of Huaiyang, Yanxiu, marry her.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Turk khan Moqi submitted a memorial saying he had a daughter and sought a marriage alliance. Wu Zetian gladly agreed and intended to have the Prince of Huaiyang, Yanxiu, marry her.

sentences.zh: 柬之奏曰：“自古無天子求娶夷狄女以配中國王者。

translations.literal: Jianzhi memorialized: "Since antiquity no Son of Heaven has sought to marry a barbarian woman's daughter to match a Chinese king.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi submitted a memorial: "Since antiquity no Son of Heaven has ever sought to take a barbarian woman's daughter as a match for a Chinese king.

sentences.zh: ”表入，頗忤其旨。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, it greatly went against her intent.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, it greatly offended her wishes.

sentences.zh: 神功初，出為合州刺史，尋轉蜀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenggong era, he was sent out as prefect of Hezhou, soon transferred to prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shenggong era he was appointed prefect of Hezhou, and soon afterward transferred to prefect of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 舊例，每歲差兵募五百人往姚州鎮守，路越山險，死者甚多。

translations.literal: By old precedent, each year five hundred conscripted soldiers were dispatched to garrison Yaozhou; the route crossed perilous mountains and many died.
translations.idiomatic: By established practice, five hundred conscripted troops were sent each year to garrison Yaozhou. The route crossed dangerous mountains, and many died along the way.

sentences.zh: 柬之表論其弊曰：

translations.literal: Jianzhi memorialized arguing its harms, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi submitted a memorial on the abuses, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣竊按姚州者，古哀牢之舊國。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully notes that Yaozhou is the old state of Ailao.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject respectfully observes that Yaozhou was the ancient state of Ailao.

sentences.zh: 絕域荒外，山高水深，自生人以來，洎於後漢，不與中國交通。

translations.literal: A remote region beyond the wilderness, with high mountains and deep waters—from the birth of humanity down to the Later Han, it had no contact with China.
translations.idiomatic: It lies in a remote wilderness beyond the frontier, with high mountains and deep waters. From the beginning of human history down to the Later Han, it had no contact with China.

sentences.zh: 前漢唐蒙開夜郎滇筰，而哀牢不附。

translations.literal: In the Former Han, Tang Meng opened Yelang, Dian, and Zuozuo, but Ailao did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the Former Han, when Tang Meng opened Yelang, Dian, and Zuozuo, Ailao still did not submit.

sentences.zh: 至光武季年，始請內屬，漢置永昌郡以統理之，乃收其鹽布毯罽之稅，以利中土。

translations.literal: Only in the final years of Emperor Guangwu did it first request incorporation; Han established Yongchang commandery to govern it and collected taxes on its salt, cloth, felt, and woolen goods to benefit the central lands.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the final years of Emperor Guangwu did it first ask to come under Han rule. The Han then established Yongchang commandery to govern it and collected taxes on salt, cloth, felt, and wool to benefit the heartland.

sentences.zh: 其國西通大秦，南通交趾，奇珍異寶，進貢歲時不闕。

translations.literal: Its state connected west to Da Qin and south to Jiaozhi; rare treasures and precious goods were sent as tribute every year without fail.
translations.idiomatic: The region connected west to Da Qin and south to Jiaozhi, and rare treasures were sent as tribute year after year without interruption.

sentences.zh: 劉備據有巴蜀，常以甲兵不充。

translations.literal: When Liu Bei held Ba and Shu, he often lacked sufficient armor and troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei held Ba and Shu, he often lacked enough armor and troops.

sentences.zh: 及備死，諸葛亮五月渡瀘，收其金銀鹽布以益軍儲，使張伯岐選其勁卒搜兵以增武備。

translations.literal: After Bei's death, Zhuge Liang crossed the Lu River in the fifth month, collected its gold, silver, salt, and cloth to augment military stores, and had Zhang Boqi select its strong soldiers to gather troops and increase armaments.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Bei died, Zhuge Liang crossed the Lu River in the fifth month, took its gold, silver, salt, and cloth to fill the army's stores, and had Zhang Boqi select strong local soldiers to raise troops and strengthen defenses.

sentences.zh: 故《蜀志》稱自亮南征之後，國以富饒，甲兵充足。

translations.literal: Therefore the Records of Shu states that after Liang's southern campaign, the state became wealthy and armor and troops were ample.
translations.idiomatic: The Records of Shu says that after Zhuge Liang's southern campaign, the state grew rich and its armor and troops were fully supplied.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，則前代置郡，其利頗深。

translations.literal: From this it follows that establishing a commandery in earlier times brought considerable benefit.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that establishing a commandery there in earlier times brought great benefit.

sentences.zh: 今鹽布之稅不供，珍奇之貢不入，戈戟之用不實於戎行，寶貨之資不輸於大國，而空竭府庫，驅率平人，受役蠻夷，肝腦塗地，臣竊為國家惜之。

translations.literal: Now taxes on salt and cloth are not supplied, tribute of rare goods does not enter, halberds and spears are not put to use in the army, treasures and goods are not delivered to the great state—yet the treasury is emptied in vain, common people are driven forth, forced to serve among the barbarians, and their lives are wasted; your subject privately grieves for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Today salt and cloth taxes are not paid, rare tribute does not arrive, weapons are not put to use in the army, and wealth is not delivered to the empire—yet the treasury is drained, common people are driven out, forced to serve among the barbarians, and left to die in the wilderness. Your subject grieves for the state.

sentences.zh: 昔漢以得利既多，曆博南山，涉蘭倉水，更置博南、哀牢二縣。

translations.literal: Formerly Han, having gained much profit, crossed Mount Bonan, forded the Lancang River, and further established the two counties of Bonan and Ailao.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, once Han had gained great profit there, it crossed Mount Bonan, forded the Lancang River, and established the counties of Bonan and Ailao.

sentences.zh: 蜀人愁怨，行者作歌曰：“曆博南，越蘭津，渡蘭蒼，為他人。

translations.literal: The people of Shu were full of grief and resentment; travelers made a song saying: "Crossing Bonan, passing Lancang Ford, fording the Lancang—working for others.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu groaned in resentment, and travelers sang: "Cross Bonan, pass Lancang Ford, ford the Lancang—for someone else's sake.

sentences.zh: ”蓋譏漢貪珍奇鹽布之利，而為蠻夷之所驅役也。

translations.literal: " This mocked Han's greed for the profit of rare goods, salt, and cloth, and for being driven to serve by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: " This mocked Han for coveting rare goods and salt-and-cloth profits, and for being driven to labor by the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 漢獲其利，人且怨歌。

translations.literal: Han gained the profit, yet the people still sang songs of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Han gained the profit, yet the people still sang songs of resentment.

sentences.zh: 今減耗國儲，費用日廣，而使陛下之赤子身膏野草，骸骨不歸，老母幼子，哀號望祭於千里之外。

translations.literal: Now national stores are depleted and expenses grow daily, yet Your Majesty's common people leave their flesh to grease the wild grasses, their bones do not return home, and old mothers and young children wail and look toward sacrifices a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: Today national stores are being drained and costs rise daily, while Your Majesty's people leave their bodies to rot in the wild, their bones never return home, and old mothers and young children wail and gaze toward distant sacrifices a thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 於國家無絲發之利，在百姓受終身之酷。

translations.literal: For the state there is not the slightest benefit; for the common people there is lifelong suffering.
translations.idiomatic: The state gains not the slightest benefit, while the people suffer cruelty that lasts a lifetime.

sentences.zh: 臣竊為國家痛之。

translations.literal: Your subject privately grieves for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject grieves deeply for the state.

sentences.zh: 往者，諸葛亮破南中，使其渠率自相統領，不置漢官，亦不留兵鎮守。

translations.literal: In the past, when Zhuge Liang conquered the Southern Center, he had the tribal chiefs govern one another, set up no Han officials, and left no troops to garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when Zhuge Liang conquered the Southern Center, he let the tribal chiefs govern one another, appointed no Han officials, and left no garrison troops behind.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，亮言置官留兵有三不易。

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, Liang said that setting up officials and leaving troops had three difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: When people asked why, Zhuge Liang said that appointing officials and leaving troops presented three serious difficulties.

sentences.zh: 大意以置官夷漢雜居，猜嫌必起；

translations.literal: In general terms, setting up officials meant barbarians and Han living mixed together, and suspicion was sure to arise;
translations.idiomatic: In essence, appointing officials meant barbarians and Han would live mixed together, and suspicion was bound to arise;

sentences.zh: 留兵運糧，為患更重；

translations.literal: leaving troops meant transporting grain, which brought even greater trouble;
translations.idiomatic: leaving troops meant transporting grain, which created even greater hardship;

sentences.zh: 忽若反叛，勞費更多。

translations.literal: if they suddenly rebelled, labor and expense would be even greater.
translations.idiomatic: if they rebelled suddenly, the labor and expense would be even greater.

sentences.zh: 但粗設紀綱，自然安定。

translations.literal: Only by setting out a rough framework of order would stability come naturally.
translations.idiomatic: Only by establishing a rough framework of order would the region settle naturally.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以亮之此策，妙得羈縻蠻夷之術。

translations.literal: Your subject privately holds that this policy of Liang's masterfully grasped the art of keeping the barbarians under loose control.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes this policy of Zhuge Liang's masterfully captured the art of keeping barbarian peoples under loose control.

sentences.zh: 今姚府所置之官，既無安邊靜寇之心，又無葛亮且縱且擒之伎。

translations.literal: The officials now set up at the Yao prefecture office have neither the mind to settle the frontier and quiet bandits, nor Zhuge Liang's skill of releasing and then capturing.
translations.idiomatic: The officials now stationed at the Yao prefecture office have neither the will to secure the frontier and pacify raiders, nor Zhuge Liang's skill of alternately releasing and capturing.

sentences.zh: 唯知詭謀狡算，恣情割剝，貪叨劫掠，積以為常。

translations.literal: They know only scheming and cunning calculation, plundering as they please, greedy for loot and robbery, making these their daily habit.
translations.idiomatic: They know only scheming and cunning, plundering as they please, greedy for loot and robbery until such conduct becomes routine.

sentences.zh: 扇動酋渠，遺成朋黨，折支諂笑，取媚蠻夷，拜跪趨伏，無復慚恥。

translations.literal: They incite tribal chiefs, leave behind factions, break themselves with fawning smiles to curry favor with the barbarians, bowing, kneeling, and scurrying forward without any shame left.
translations.idiomatic: They stir up tribal chiefs, form cliques, grovel and flatter to win favor with the barbarians, bowing and kneeling without a trace of shame.

sentences.zh: 提挈子弟，嘯引凶愚，聚會蒲博，一擲累萬。

translations.literal: They drag along younger relatives, rally the vicious and foolish, gather for gambling, and stake tens of thousands on a single throw.
translations.idiomatic: They drag along younger relatives, rally the vicious and foolish, gather for gambling, and stake tens of thousands on a single throw.

sentences.zh: 劍南逋逃，中原亡命，有二千餘戶，見散在彼州，專以掠奪為業。

translations.literal: Fugitives from Jiannan and outlaws from the central plains, more than two thousand households, are now scattered in that prefecture, making plunder their sole occupation.
translations.idiomatic: More than two thousand households of fugitives from Jiannan and outlaws from the central plains are now scattered through that prefecture, making plunder their sole occupation.

sentences.zh: 姚州本龍朔中武陵縣主簿石子仁奏置之，後長史李孝讓、辛文協並為群蠻所殺。

translations.literal: Yaozhou was originally established on the memorial of Shi Ziren, registrar of Wuling county, in the Longshuo era; later the chief administrators Li Xiaorang and Xin Wenxie were both killed by the barbarian bands.
translations.idiomatic: Yaozhou was originally established on a memorial submitted in the Longshuo era by Shi Ziren, registrar of Wuling county. Later the chief administrators Li Xiaorang and Xin Wenxie were both killed by barbarian bands.

sentences.zh: 前朝遣郎將趙武貴討擊，貴及蜀兵應時破敗，噍類無遺。

translations.literal: The previous court sent General Zhao Wugui to attack; Wugui and the Shu troops were promptly defeated, and not one mouth was left.
translations.idiomatic: The previous court sent General Zhao Wugui to attack, but he and the Shu troops were promptly defeated, and not one survivor was left.

sentences.zh: 又使將軍李義總等往征，郎將劉惠基在陣戰死，其州乃廢。

translations.literal: The court again sent General Li Yizong and others to campaign; General Liu Huiji died in battle, and the prefecture was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The court again sent General Li Yizong and others to campaign, but General Liu Huiji died in battle and the prefecture was abolished.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以諸葛亮稱置官留兵有三不易，其言乃驗。

translations.literal: Your subject privately holds that Zhuge Liang's saying that setting up officials and leaving troops had three difficulties has indeed been verified.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes Zhuge Liang's warning that appointing officials and leaving troops had three serious difficulties has been borne out.

sentences.zh: 至垂拱四年，蠻郎將王善寶、昆州刺史爨乾福又請置州，奏言所有課稅，自出姚府管內，更不勞擾蜀中。

translations.literal: By the fourth year of the Chuigong era, the barbarian general Wang Shanbao and the prefect of Kunzhou, Cuan Qianfu, again requested establishment of the prefecture, memorializing that all taxes and levies would come from within the jurisdiction of the Yao prefecture office and would no longer trouble Shu.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth year of the Chuigong era, the barbarian general Wang Shanbao and Kunzhou prefect Cuan Qianfu again requested that the prefecture be established, stating that all taxes and levies would be raised within the Yao prefecture's jurisdiction and would no longer burden Shu.

sentences.zh: 及置州後，錄事參軍李棱為蠻所殺。

translations.literal: After the prefecture was established, the recording secretary Li Leng was killed by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: After the prefecture was reestablished, the recording secretary Li Leng was killed by the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 延載中，司馬成琛奏請於瀘南置鎮七所，遣蜀兵防守，自此蜀中騷擾，於今不息。

translations.literal: In the Yanzai era, Sima Chengchen memorialized requesting establishment of seven garrisons south of the Lu River and dispatch of Shu troops to defend them; from then on Shu was disturbed, and to this day the turmoil has not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanzai era, Sima Chengchen submitted a memorial requesting seven garrisons south of the Lu River and the dispatch of Shu troops to guard them. From that time Shu fell into unrest, and the disturbance has not ceased to this day.

sentences.zh: 且姚府總管五十七州，巨猾遊客，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Yao prefecture office governs fifty-seven prefectures, with great scoundrels and roaming adventurers beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Yao prefecture office oversees fifty-seven prefectures, and great scoundrels and roaming adventurers are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 國家設官分職，本以化俗妨奸，無恥無厭，狼籍至此。

translations.literal: The state sets up officials and divides duties precisely to transform customs and prevent wrongdoing, yet these men are shameless and insatiable, leaving disorder spread to this extent.
translations.idiomatic: The state appoints officials and divides duties precisely to reform customs and check wrongdoing, yet these men are shameless and insatiable, and have reduced the region to such disorder.

sentences.zh: 今不問夷夏，負罪並深，見道路劫殺，不能禁止，恐一旦驚擾，為禍轉大。

translations.literal: Now without distinction between barbarian and Chinese, all are deeply guilty; robbery and murder are seen on the roads and cannot be stopped—I fear that if alarm and disturbance break out suddenly, the disaster will grow even greater.
translations.idiomatic: Today, without distinction between barbarians and Chinese, all are deeply guilty. Robbery and murder occur on the roads and cannot be stopped. I fear that if unrest breaks out suddenly, the disaster will grow far worse.

sentences.zh: 伏乞省罷姚州，使隸巂府，歲時朝覲，同之蕃國。

translations.literal: I humbly beg that Yaozhou be abolished and placed under Xi prefecture, with seasonal court audiences treated like those of tributary states.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that Yaozhou be abolished and placed under Xi prefecture, with seasonal court audiences handled like those of tributary states.

sentences.zh: 瀘南諸鎮，亦皆悉廢，於瀘北置關，百姓自非奉使入蕃，不許交通往來。

translations.literal: All garrisons south of the Lu River should likewise be abolished entirely; a pass should be set up north of the Lu River, and common people, unless on official mission into the barbarian lands, should not be permitted to travel back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: All garrisons south of the Lu River should likewise be abolished, a pass established north of the Lu River, and ordinary people forbidden to travel into barbarian territory except on official missions.

sentences.zh: 增巂府兵選，擇清良宰牧以統理之。

translations.literal: Increase the selection of troops for Xi prefecture and choose upright and worthy administrators to govern the region.
translations.idiomatic: Increase the selection of troops for Xi prefecture and appoint upright, capable administrators to govern the region.

sentences.zh: 臣愚將為穩便。

translations.literal: Your subject's humble opinion is that this would be the stable and suitable course.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes this would be the stable and prudent course.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，則天不納。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Wu Zetian did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Wu Zetian rejected it.

sentences.zh: 後累拜荊州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Later he was repeatedly appointed chief administrator of the Jingzhou Grand Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed chief administrator of the Jingzhou Grand Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 長安中，召為司刑少卿，遷秋官侍郎。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, he was summoned as vice minister of justice and promoted to vice minister of the autumn office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he was summoned to serve as vice minister of justice and later promoted to vice minister of the autumn office.

sentences.zh: 時夏官尚書姚崇為靈武軍使，將行，則天令舉外司堪為宰相者。

translations.literal: At that time Summer Office Minister Yao Chong was military commissioner of Lingwu and about to depart; Wu Zetian ordered recommendations of officials outside the central administration who were fit to serve as chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Summer Office Minister Yao Chong was about to depart as military commissioner of Lingwu, and Wu Zetian ordered recommendations of officials outside the central administration who were fit to serve as chancellors.

sentences.zh: 崇對曰：“張柬之沉厚有謀，能斷大事，且其人年老，惟陛下急用之。

translations.literal: Chong replied: "Zhang Jianzhi is steady and deep, full of strategy, able to decide great affairs, and moreover he is old in years—Your Majesty should use him urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied: "Zhang Jianzhi is steady and shrewd, capable of deciding great affairs, and he is already advanced in years. Your Majesty should appoint him at once.

sentences.zh: ”則天登時召見，尋同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: " Wu Zetian immediately summoned him for audience, and soon he became associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Platform.
translations.idiomatic: " Wu Zetian summoned him immediately, and soon afterward he was made associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Platform.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷鳳閣侍郎，仍知政事。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to vice director of the Phoenix Pavilion and continued to manage state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to vice director of the Phoenix Pavilion and continued to manage state affairs.

sentences.zh: 及誅張易之兄弟，柬之首謀其事。

translations.literal: When the Zhang Yizhi brothers were executed, Jianzhi was the chief planner of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhang Yizhi brothers were executed, Jianzhi was the chief planner of the coup.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，以功擢拜天官尚書、鳳閣鸞台三品，封漢陽郡公，食實封五百戶，未幾，遷中書令，監修國史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, for his merit he was promoted to minister of the heaven office and third rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Platform, enfeoffed as Duke of Hanyang with five hundred taxable households, and before long transferred to director of the Secretariat and supervisor of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, Jianzhi was promoted for his merit to minister of the heaven office and third rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Platform, enfeoffed as Duke of Hanyang with five hundred taxable households, and soon afterward made director of the Secretariat and supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 月餘，進封漢陽郡王，加授特進，令罷知政事。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month, he was advanced to Prince of Hanyang commandery, granted special advancement, and ordered to cease managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a month he was advanced to Prince of Hanyang commandery, granted special advancement, and relieved of his duties in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 玄孫璟，開成二年，自宜城尉遷壽安尉。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandson Jing, in the second year of Kaicheng, was transferred from magistrate of Yicheng to magistrate of Shou'an.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandson Jing was transferred from magistrate of Yicheng to magistrate of Shou'an in the second year of Kaicheng.

sentences.zh: 袁恕己，滄州東光人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Shuji was a native of Dongguang in Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shuji was a native of Dongguang in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 長安中，曆遷司刑少卿，兼知相王府司馬事。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, he was promoted through the ranks to vice minister of justice and concurrently managed the affairs of the Prince of Xiang's palace marshal.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he rose to vice minister of justice and concurrently managed affairs as marshal of the Prince of Xiang's household.

sentences.zh: 敬暉等將誅張易之兄弟，恕己預其謀議，又從相王統率南衙兵仗，以備非常。

translations.literal: When Jing Hui and the others were about to execute the Zhang Yizhi brothers, Shuji took part in their planning, and also followed the Prince of Xiang in commanding the southern palace troops and arms to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Hui and the others planned to execute the Zhang Yizhi brothers, Shuji joined their deliberations and followed the Prince of Xiang in commanding the southern palace troops and arms against any emergency.

sentences.zh: 及事定，加銀青光祿大夫，行中書侍郎、同中書門下三品，封南陽郡公，食實封五百戶。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was given the silver-blue gleaming grand master of splendid happiness, acting vice director of the Secretariat and third rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery, enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang with five hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, he was granted silver-blue gleaming grand master of splendid happiness, acting vice director of the Secretariat and third rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang with five hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 將作少匠楊務廉素以工巧見用，中興初，恕己恐其更啟遊娛侈靡之端，言於中宗曰：“務廉致位九卿，積有歲年，苦言嘉謀，無足可紀。

translations.literal: Assistant director of palace construction Yang Wulian had long been employed for his craftsmanship; at the beginning of the restoration, Shuji feared he would again open the way to pleasure-seeking and extravagant excess, and said to Emperor Zhongzong: "Wulian has risen to one of the nine ministers and accumulated years in office, yet earnest counsel and fine plans from him are not worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant director of palace construction Yang Wulian had long been valued for his craftsmanship. At the beginning of the restoration, Shuji feared he would again open the way to pleasure and extravagance, and said to Emperor Zhongzong: "Wulian has risen to one of the nine ministers and served for many years, yet he has offered no earnest counsel or fine plan worth recording.

sentences.zh: 每宮室營構，必務其侈，若不斥之，何以廣昭聖德？

translations.literal: Whenever palace buildings are constructed, he always pursues extravagance—if he is not dismissed, how can Your Majesty's sagely virtue be broadly displayed?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever palace buildings are constructed, he always pursues extravagance. If he is not dismissed, how can Your Majesty's sagely virtue be broadly displayed?

sentences.zh: ”由是左授務廉陵州刺史。

translations.literal: " On this account Wulian was demoted and appointed prefect of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " On this account Wulian was demoted to prefect of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 恕己俄擢拜中書令，仍加特進，封南陽郡王，罷知政事。

translations.literal: Shuji was soon promoted to director of the Secretariat, additionally granted special advancement, enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang commandery, and relieved of managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shuji was soon promoted to director of the Secretariat, granted special advancement, enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang commandery, and relieved of his duties in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 則天崩，遺製加實封滿七百戶。

translations.literal: When Wu Zetian died, her final edict added taxable households until the total reached seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zetian died, her final edict increased his taxable households to seven hundred.

sentences.zh: 後與敬暉等累遭貶黜，流於環州。

translations.literal: Later he and Jing Hui and the others were repeatedly demoted and exiled to Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Jing Hui and the others were repeatedly demoted and exiled to Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋為周利貞所逼，飲野葛汁數升，恕己常服黃金，餌毒發，憤悶，以手掘地，取土而食，爪甲殆盡，竟不死，乃擊殺之。

translations.literal: Soon he was pressed by Zhou Lizhen and forced to drink several sheng of wild kudzu juice; Shuji habitually took gold, the poison took effect, and in rage and distress he dug at the ground with his hands, eating the soil until his fingernails were nearly gone; he still did not die, and so was beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhou Lizhen forced him to drink several sheng of wild kudzu poison. Shuji habitually took gold, so when the poison took effect he fell into rage and distress, dug at the ground with his hands, and ate the soil until his fingernails were nearly gone. He still did not die, and so was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 建中初，贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, he was posthumously given the title of grand tutor of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era he was posthumously granted the title of grand tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 曾孫德文，舉進士，開成三年，授秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Dewen passed the jinshi examination; in the third year of Kaicheng he was appointed collator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Dewen passed the jinshi examination and in the third year of Kaicheng was appointed collator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔夫差入越，勾踐保於會稽，不聽子胥之言，而有甬東之歎。

translations.literal: The historian says: In former times Fuchai entered Yue and Goujian took refuge at Kuaiji; because he did not heed Zixu's words, he came to the lament of Yongdong.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Long ago, when Fuchai invaded Yue, Goujian took refuge at Kuaiji. Because he did not heed Wu Zixu's counsel, he ended with the lament of exile to Yongdong.

sentences.zh: 此五王除凶返正，得計成功。

translations.literal: These five princes removed the wicked and restored the right, achieving success through sound planning.
translations.idiomatic: These five princes removed the wicked and restored legitimate rule, achieving success through sound planning.

sentences.zh: 當是時，彥範、敬暉握兵全勢，三思、攸暨其黨半殲，若從季昶之言，寧有利貞之禍？

translations.literal: At that time Yanfan and Jing Hui held full military power; Sansi and Youji and their faction were half destroyed—if they had followed Ji Chang's words, would there have been Lizhen's disaster?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yanfan and Jing Hui held full military power, and Sansi, Youji, and their faction were half destroyed. If they had followed Ji Chang's advice, would they have suffered Zhou Lizhen's disaster?

sentences.zh: 蓋以心懷不忍，遽失後圖，黜削流移，理固然也。

translations.literal: It was because their hearts could not bear to go further that they suddenly lost their later plans; demotion, stripping of rank, and exile were naturally to be expected.
translations.idiomatic: Because their hearts could not bear to go further, they suddenly lost their later plans. Demotion, stripping of rank, and exile were only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 且芟蔓而不能拔本，建謀而尚欠防微，死即無辜，禍由自掇。

translations.literal: Moreover, they cut the creepers but could not uproot the root; they formed plans yet still fell short in guarding against the first signs of trouble—though their deaths were undeserved, the disaster was of their own drawing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, they cut the creepers but failed to uproot the root. They formed plans yet still neglected to guard against trouble at its first signs. Though their deaths were undeserved, they brought the disaster on themselves.

sentences.zh: 失斷召亂也，不亦宜哉！

translations.literal: Failure in decisive action invites disorder—is this not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Failure to act decisively invites disorder—is this not exactly what one would expect!

sentences.zh: 讚曰：嗟彼五王，忠於有唐。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Alas for those five princes, loyal to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Alas for those five princes, loyal to Tang.

sentences.zh: 知火在木，謂其無傷。

translations.literal: Knowing fire was in the wood, they thought it would do no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing fire in the wood, they thought it would do no harm.

sentences.zh: 禍發既克，勢摧靡當。

translations.literal: Once disaster broke out they were overcome, and their power was crushed beyond resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Once disaster broke out they were overcome, and their power was crushed beyond resistance.

sentences.zh: 何事不敏，周身之防。

translations.literal: In what matter were they not remiss? They lacked thorough protection for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In what matter were they not remiss? They failed to guard themselves thoroughly.
